# DAG Execution Engine — EPIC design (for codex review)

**Status**: DRAFT for codex adversarial review (2026-05-24). No code yet.
**Origin**: 3-way audit (me + sub-agent + codex, all verdict TRUE) found the
firmware-DAG executor (path a) is unimplemented. Audit + memory:
`project_dag_execution_engine_unimplemented`, codex audit
`docs/audit/codex-reviews/dag-execution-engine-audit-codex-2026-05-24.txt`.
**Decision to scope this** (operator, 2026-05-24): treat the firmware-DAG as a
committed capability and produce the full EPIC design + 1-3wk scope.

## 1. Problem & framing
There are TWO independent "DAG" paths in the codebase:
- **(a) DAG-plan path** — `POST /api/v1/dag` → `workflow.start(dag=…)` validates +
  persists to `dag_plans` + marks `executing`, **then stops**. No executor runs the
  tasks (compile/flash/cross-compile/package); nothing sets `completed` or calls
  `workflow.finish()` from an executor. This EPIC builds path (a).
- **(b) Orchestration path** — JIRA webhook → `orchestrator_gateway.build_catcs_from_dag`
  → `queue_backend` → `worker.py` → `run_graph` → Gerrit. **Already works**
  (the live code-authoring pipeline). NOT touched by this EPIC, but its sandbox
  runtime + queue/claim patterns are the reuse substrate.

**Goal**: a `/api/v1/dag` submission of `smoke-compile-flash-host-native` (and, in
later phases, cross-compile/package/remote-board DAGs) **executes its tasks to
`completed`**, records `workflow_steps`, and greens `staging-gate-smoke` honestly.

**Non-goals**: replacing path (b); building a new UI; multi-tenant canary (Boreas-B
Gap B, deferred). The smoke gate is NOT a live promote blocker today (canary is the
operative gate; `staging-gate-smoke.timer` is `not-found`), so this is a
capability + fidelity build, not a hotfix.

## 2. Reusable substrate (confirmed by audit — do NOT rebuild)

|---|---|---|

| `dag_validator` | backend/dag_validator.py | already gates submit (cycles/MECE/tier) |
| `dag_storage` state machine | backend/dag_storage.py:54 | `executing→completed` already LEGAL; `set_status` has FOR UPDATE row-lock; lookups by id/run_id |
| `workflow.step(run, idempotency_key)` | backend/workflow.py:538 | durable append-only checkpoint; `(run_id, idempotency_key)` UNIQUE → idempotent replay; `task_id` is part of the key |
| `workflow.finish(run_id, status)` | backend/workflow.py:340 | terminal run transition |
| `container.dispatch_t3 / start_container / exec_in_container` | backend/container.py:930/585/986 | sandbox exec primitives |
| `t3_resolver.resolve_t3_runner` | backend/t3_resolver.py:109 | LOCAL vs BUNDLE/SSH decision (host_native → LOCAL) |
| `ssh_runner.run_on_target` | backend/ssh_runner.py | real remote-board exec (t3 BUNDLE) |
| `sandbox_prewarm` | backend/sandbox_prewarm.py | topo-orders + pre-warms in-degree-0 tasks (reuse the topo walk) |
| `SandboxRuntime` protocol (`LocalSandboxRuntime`) | backend/worker.py:205 | prepare/run sandbox; path-b's executor substrate |

## 3. Target architecture
A **DAG executor** that turns an `executing` plan into a completed run:

```
[plan claimer] → [topo scheduler] → [task dispatch] → [handler] → [step record] → [terminal wiring]
  poll/claim       ready set          by toolchain     compile/    workflow.step    set_status(completed)
  executing        honor depends_on   + required_tier  flash/...   (idempotent)     + workflow.finish
```

### Components (each ≈ a child Story)
- **E1 — Plan claimer / executor loop.** Poll `dag_plans WHERE status='executing'`,
  claim with a lease so multi-replica backends/workers don't double-run. Reuse the
  OP-977 fencing-token pattern (`claim:{instance}:{epoch}-{uuid}`, lowest-token-wins)
  or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Lease renew + reclaim on crash.
- **E2 — Topological scheduler.** Build the ready-set from `depends_on` (reuse
  `sandbox_prewarm`'s indegree walk), run ready tasks (bounded concurrency within a
  plan), advance as deps complete. Fail-fast vs continue-on-error policy.
- **E3 — Task-type → handler dispatch.** Registry keyed on `toolchain` × `required_tier`.
  t1 = local sandbox container; networked = sandbox + egress; t3 = `t3_resolver` →
  LOCAL (host-native, same arch/OS) or BUNDLE/SSH (`ssh_runner`). **CLAUDE.md rule:
  cross-compile MUST use the platform toolchain from `get_platform_config` +
  `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` + `--sysroot` — never system gcc.**
- **E4 — Task handlers.** `compile` (cmake/make/host gcc; cross via platform
  toolchain), `flash` (host_native LOCAL = symbolic/no-op-to-loopback; real device =
  `ssh_runner`/hardware bridge), `package`, `cross-compile`. Each runs the task's
  `toolchain` command in a workspace, captures rc/stdout/artifact at `expected_output`.
- **E5 — Step recording + artifact check.** One `workflow.step` per task (idempotency
  key includes `task_id`); validate `expected_output` produced; link
  `workflow_steps.dag_task_id`.
- **E6 — Terminal wiring.** All tasks ok → `set_status(plan,'completed')` +
  `workflow.finish(run,'completed')`. Any fail → `failed` + finish `failed`/`halted`
  (+ optional Phase 56-DAG-C mutation hook).
- **E7 — Failure / retry / crash-resume.** Idempotent re-claim skips done steps (via
  `workflow.step` UNIQUE); per-task retry policy; poison-plan handling.
- **E8 — Side-effect isolation.** Dev/staging MUST NOT touch prod artifacts/registry/
  Gerrit/real hardware. Env-gated handler "test mode" (symbolic flash, scratch
  workspace, no push). Ties to A2 env-contract.
- **E9 — Deployment.** Decide: in-process lifespan task gated by
  `OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_ENABLED` vs a separate worker container/systemd unit
  (mirror `omnisight-worker@`). Wire onto staging; re-green `staging-gate-smoke`;
  re-enable the timer. 4-AC + Go-Live.
- **E10 — Observability + honesty pass.** Executor heartbeat/metrics; fix misleading
  surfaces (`TODO.md:131` "2 real DAGs end-to-end"; any `/api/v1/dag`-as-executable
  product copy).

## 4. Phasing & effort (3-way consensus)
- **Phase 1 — Smoke MVP (~2-5 person-days, MEDIUM risk).** E1(single-claim) + E2 +
  E3/E4 for host-native `compile`+`flash` only (LocalSandboxRuntime, symbolic flash)
  + E5 + E6 happy-path + E8 test-mode. Outcome: `smoke-compile-flash-host-native`
  reaches `completed`; smoke gate greens for real on staging.
- **Phase 2 — Tier expansion (~1 week).** cross-compile (platform toolchain rule) +
  package + t3 BUNDLE/SSH remote-board via `ssh_runner`; the second smoke DAG
  (`smoke-cross-compile-aarch64`).
- **Phase 3 — Production hardening (~1 week).** Multi-replica claim/fencing (E1 full),
  retry/crash-resume (E7), failure semantics, full side-effect isolation, metrics.
- **Total: ~1-3 weeks** depending on how far past MVP.

## 5. Open questions for codex
1. **In-process vs separate worker (E9).** A lifespan background task in the staging
   backend is simplest but couples executor lifecycle to the API process + multiplies
   across replicas (a/b) → needs claim even for MVP. A separate worker
   (mirror `omnisight-worker@`) is cleaner isolation but more infra. Which for MVP?
2. **Should path (a) and path (b) converge?** Both use `dag_schema.DAG` + a sandbox
   runtime. Is building a *second* executor the right call, or should path-a DAGs be
   lowered into path-b TaskCards (reuse `worker.py` + queue) so there's ONE execution
   substrate? Trade-off: reuse vs the two having different semantics (dag_plans
   lifecycle + workflow_steps vs CATC queue + Gerrit push).
3. **What does host-native `flash` even mean (E4)?** On a server there's no device.
   Is symbolic/no-op flash an honest "completed", or does that make the smoke gate
   test a hollow path? Should the smoke DAG be redefined to something with real
   host-native semantics (compile + run-tests) instead of compile+flash?
4. **Claim mechanism for MVP (E1).** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (DB-native, simple) vs
   the OP-977 fencing-token pattern (already in-codebase for runners). Given staging
   has backend-a + backend-b, even MVP needs *some* claim — which?
5. **Side-effect isolation (E8).** Is an env flag (`OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_TEST_MODE`)
   enough, or must handlers hard-refuse prod artifact/registry/Gerrit endpoints when
   `OMNISIGHT_ENV != prod` (defense-in-depth like the A2 contract)?
6. **Is this worth building at all** given the runner-as-product pivot — i.e. is the
   firmware compile/flash capability still strategically wanted, or should Phase 1
   stop at "smoke greens" and the rest stay parked? (Operator already chose to scope
   it; codex: sanity-check whether the EPIC over-builds vs the actual product need.)
7. **MECE / artifact collisions** on a shared staging workspace across concurrent
   plans (E2/E8) — does `expected_output` + `output_overlap_ack` suffice, or is
   per-plan workspace isolation required from day 1?

     1	"""Phase 56-DAG-A — DAG schema for the self-healing planner.
     2	
     3	Pydantic models that mirror the Orchestrator template's JSON contract
     4	(`docs/design/self-healing-scheduling-mechanism.md` §三). Schema-level
     5	validation runs automatically on `DAG.model_validate(payload)`. The
     6	**semantic** rules (cycles, tier capability, MECE, dep closure, I/O
     7	entity) live in `backend/dag_validator.py` so they can be invoked
     8	once and produce a list of all errors at once instead of failing on
     9	the first.
    10	
    11	`schema_version: int = 1` lets us evolve without breaking historic
    12	plans stored in `dag_plans` (Phase 56-DAG-B).
    13	"""
    14	
    15	from __future__ import annotations
    16	
    17	from typing import Literal, Optional
    18	
    19	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
    20	
    21	
    22	TierId = Literal["t1", "networked", "t3"]
    23	SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
    24	
    25	
    26	class Task(BaseModel):
    27	    """One node in the DAG."""
    28	
    29	    task_id: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=64)
    30	    description: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=4000)
    31	
    32	    required_tier: TierId
    33	    toolchain: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128)
    34	
    35	    inputs: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    36	    expected_output: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=512)
    37	    depends_on: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    38	
    39	    # Phase 56-DAG-A — explicit MECE escape hatch. Two tasks may share
    40	    # an `expected_output` only when BOTH set this to True (e.g. parallel
    41	    # benchmark runs writing the same report path that's later merged).
    42	    output_overlap_ack: bool = False
    43	
    44	    @field_validator("task_id")
    45	    @classmethod
    46	    def _id_is_simple(cls, v: str) -> str:
    47	        # Keep id printable — used as Decision Engine key + as part of
    48	        # workflow_steps.idempotency_key (Phase 56-DAG-B).
    49	        if not v.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
    50	            raise ValueError(
    51	                "task_id must be alphanumeric / dash / underscore only"
    52	            )
    53	        return v
    54	
    55	    @field_validator("depends_on")
    56	    @classmethod
    57	    def _no_self_dep(cls, v: list[str], info) -> list[str]:
    58	        tid = info.data.get("task_id")
    59	        if tid and tid in v:
    60	            raise ValueError(f"task {tid!r} cannot depend on itself")
    61	        if len(v) != len(set(v)):
    62	            raise ValueError("depends_on must not contain duplicates")
    63	        return v
    64	
    65	
    66	class DAG(BaseModel):
    67	    """The full planning artefact."""
    68	
    69	    schema_version: int = SCHEMA_VERSION
    70	    dag_id: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=64)
    71	    total_tasks: Optional[int] = None
    72	    tasks: list[Task]
    73	
    74	    @field_validator("schema_version")
    75	    @classmethod
    76	    def _supported_version(cls, v: int) -> int:
    77	        if v != SCHEMA_VERSION:
    78	            # Keep simple for v1; raise instead of silent migrate.
    79	            raise ValueError(
    80	                f"unsupported schema_version {v} (expected {SCHEMA_VERSION})"
    81	            )
    82	        return v
    83	
    84	    @field_validator("tasks")
    85	    @classmethod
    86	    def _at_least_one(cls, v: list[Task]) -> list[Task]:
    87	        if not v:
    88	            raise ValueError("DAG must have at least one task")
    89	        return v

    81	def _resolve_target_profile(explicit: str | None) -> dict | None:
    82	    from pathlib import Path
    83	    import yaml as _yaml
    84	    from backend.sdk_provisioner import _validate_platform_name, _platform_profile
    85	
    86	    # 1. Explicit request field.
    87	    if explicit:
    88	        name = explicit.strip()
    89	    else:
    90	        name = ""
    91	
    92	    # 2. Fall back to hardware_manifest.
    93	    if not name:
    94	        manifest = Path("configs") / "hardware_manifest.yaml"
    95	        if manifest.is_file():
    96	            try:
    97	                m = _yaml.safe_load(manifest.read_text()) or {}
    98	                name = (
    99	                    (m.get("project") or {}).get("target_platform")
   100	                    or m.get("target_platform")
   101	                    or ""
   102	                ).strip()
   103	            except Exception as exc:
   104	                logger.debug("hardware_manifest parse failed: %s", exc)
   105	
   106	    # 3. Final default matches T1-A.
   107	    if not name:
   108	        name = "host_native"
   109	
   110	    if not _validate_platform_name(name):
   111	        logger.debug("target_platform %r rejected by validator", name)
   112	        return None
   113	    profile_path = _platform_profile(name)
   114	    if profile_path is None or not profile_path.exists():
   115	        logger.debug("target_platform %r: no profile YAML", name)
   116	        return None
   117	    try:
   118	        return _yaml.safe_load(profile_path.read_text()) or {}
   119	    except Exception as exc:
   120	        logger.debug("profile %s parse failed: %s", name, exc)
   121	        return None

   538	def step(run: WorkflowRun, idempotency_key: str):
   539	    """Decorator: wrap an async callable so it only runs once per
   540	    (run, key). On second call with the same key, returns the cached
   541	    output without invoking the body.
   542	
   543	    Use distinct keys for genuinely separate work (`fetch_repo`,
   544	    `compile/<sha>`, `push/<branch>`); reuse the same key when you
   545	    want exactly-once semantics across crash-and-resume.
   546	    """
   547	    def decorator(fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
   548	        async def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   549	            cached = await _get_step(run.id, idempotency_key)
   550	            if cached and cached.is_done:
   551	                logger.info("workflow.step cache-hit run=%s key=%s", run.id, idempotency_key)
   552	                return cached.output
   553	            try:
   554	                result = await fn(*args, **kwargs)
   555	            except Exception as exc:
   556	                # Record the failure (so we can audit / inspect)
   557	                await _record_step(run.id, idempotency_key, output=None,
   558	                                   error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc!s}"[:512])
   559	                raise
   560	            await _record_step(run.id, idempotency_key, output=result, error=None)
   561	            return result
   562	        return wrapper
   563	    return decorator

   590	    }

     7	Status state-machine (no skips, no reverse transitions):
     8	
     9	       (DAG submitted)
    10	              │
    11	              ▼
    12	          pending ──────► validated ──────► executing ──────► completed
    13	              │                                  │

    17	                                                 ▼

    21	wrapper to native asyncpg pool. ``set_status`` and ``attach_to_run``

   119	        json.dumps([e.to_dict() for e in validation_errors])
   120	        if validation_errors else None
   121	    )
   122	    row = await conn.fetchrow(
   123	        "INSERT INTO dag_plans "
   124	        "(dag_id, run_id, parent_plan_id, json_body, status, "
   125	        "mutation_round, validation_errors, created_at, updated_at) "
   126	        "VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9) RETURNING id",
   127	        dag.dag_id, run_id, parent_plan_id, dag.model_dump_json(),
   128	        status, mutation_round, err_json, now, now,
   129	    )
   130	    return row["id"]

   133	async def save_plan(
   134	    dag: DAG, *,
   135	    run_id: Optional[str] = None,
   136	    parent_plan_id: Optional[int] = None,
   137	    status: str = "pending",
   138	    mutation_round: int = 0,
   139	    validation_errors: Optional[list[DagValidationError]] = None,
   140	    conn=None,
   141	) -> StoredPlan:
   142	    """Insert a fresh plan row. Use `set_status` for transitions."""
   143	    if status not in _VALID_STATUSES:
   144	        raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
   145	    if conn is None:
   146	        async with get_pool().acquire() as owned:
   147	            new_id = await _save_plan_impl(
   148	                owned, dag, run_id, parent_plan_id,
   149	                status, mutation_round, validation_errors,
   150	            )
   151	    else:
   152	        new_id = await _save_plan_impl(
   153	            conn, dag, run_id, parent_plan_id,
   154	            status, mutation_round, validation_errors,
   155	        )
   156	    logger.info(
   157	        "dag plan saved id=%s dag=%s status=%s round=%d",
   158	        new_id, dag.dag_id, status, mutation_round,
   159	    )
   160	    return await get_plan(new_id, conn=conn)
   161	
   162	
   163	async def get_plan(plan_id: int, conn=None) -> StoredPlan:
   164	    sql = f"SELECT {_PLAN_COLS} FROM dag_plans WHERE id = $1"
   165	    if conn is None:
   166	        async with get_pool().acquire() as owned:
   167	            row = await owned.fetchrow(sql, plan_id)
   168	    else:
   169	        row = await conn.fetchrow(sql, plan_id)
   170	    if not row:
   171	        raise LookupError(f"no dag_plan id={plan_id}")
   172	    return _row_to_plan(row)

   175	async def get_plan_by_run(
   176	    run_id: str, conn=None,
   177	) -> Optional[StoredPlan]:
   178	    """Latest plan attached to a workflow_run (latest = highest id =
   179	    most recent mutation round)."""
   180	    sql = (
   181	        f"SELECT {_PLAN_COLS} FROM dag_plans WHERE run_id = $1 "
   182	        "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
   183	    )
   184	    if conn is None:
   185	        async with get_pool().acquire() as owned:
   186	            row = await owned.fetchrow(sql, run_id)
   187	    else:
   188	        row = await conn.fetchrow(sql, run_id)
   189	    return _row_to_plan(row) if row else None

   192	async def list_plans(
   193	    dag_id: str, conn=None,
   194	) -> list[StoredPlan]:
   195	    """All plans for one logical DAG, ordered by mutation round."""
   196	    sql = (
   197	        f"SELECT {_PLAN_COLS} FROM dag_plans WHERE dag_id = $1 "
   198	        "ORDER BY mutation_round, id"
   199	    )
   200	    if conn is None:
   201	        async with get_pool().acquire() as owned:
   202	            rows = await owned.fetch(sql, dag_id)
   203	    else:
   204	        rows = await conn.fetch(sql, dag_id)
   205	    return [_row_to_plan(r) for r in rows]

   207	
   208	async def _set_status_impl(
   209	    conn, plan_id: int, new_status: str, run_id: Optional[str],
   210	) -> None:
   211	    # SELECT FOR UPDATE holds a row-level lock for the duration of the
   212	    # tx — concurrent set_status on the same plan_id serialise on the
   213	    # lock. Without it, two callers could both read status=validated,
   214	    # both compute "validated → executing is legal", both UPDATE; the
   215	    # double-transition is technically idempotent but produces
   216	    # surprising ordering in timestamps and logs.
   217	    row = await conn.fetchrow(
   218	        "SELECT status FROM dag_plans WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
   219	        plan_id,
   220	    )
   221	    if not row:
   222	        raise LookupError(f"no dag_plan id={plan_id}")
   223	    current = row["status"]
   224	    if new_status not in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[current]:
   225	        raise ValueError(
   226	            f"illegal transition {current!r} → {new_status!r} "
   227	            f"(allowed: {sorted(_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[current])})"
   228	        )
   229	    now = time.time()
   230	    if run_id is not None:
   231	        await conn.execute(
   232	            "UPDATE dag_plans SET status = $1, run_id = $2, "
   233	            "updated_at = $3 WHERE id = $4",
   234	            new_status, run_id, now, plan_id,
   235	        )
   236	    else:
   237	        await conn.execute(
   238	            "UPDATE dag_plans SET status = $1, updated_at = $2 "
   239	            "WHERE id = $3",
   240	            new_status, now, plan_id,
   241	        )
   242	
   243	
   244	async def set_status(
   245	    plan_id: int, new_status: str, *,
   246	    run_id: Optional[str] = None, conn=None,
   247	) -> StoredPlan:
   248	    """Transition status; refuses illegal moves. Optionally attach
   249	    `run_id` (used when 'pending' → 'executing' to bind a new run).
   250	
   251	    SP-5.1 (2026-04-21): the SELECT-then-UPDATE is now wrapped in a
   252	    transaction with ``SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`` — under SQLite the
   253	    file-lock serialised callers implicitly; under asyncpg pool two
   254	    concurrent set_status on the same plan could both read the same
   255	    status and both issue UPDATEs, making the ordering ambiguous.
   256	    FOR UPDATE makes it deterministic.
   257	    """
   258	    if new_status not in _VALID_STATUSES:
   259	        raise ValueError(f"unknown status {new_status!r}")
   260	    if conn is None:

   287	@router.post("")
   288	async def submit_dag(req: DAGSubmitRequest,
   289	                     _user=Depends(_au.require_operator)) -> dict:
   290	    """Submit a DAG. Validates, optionally mutates, persists, links
   291	    to a new workflow_run. Returns the run_id + plan_id + status."""
   292	    # 1. Pydantic schema on the raw JSON — reject shape errors early.
   293	    try:
   294	        dag = DAG.model_validate(req.dag)
   295	    except Exception as exc:
   296	        return JSONResponse(
   297	            status_code=422,
   298	            content={
   299	                "detail": f"DAG schema validation failed: {exc}",
   300	                "stage": "schema",
   301	            },
   302	        )
   303	
   304	    # 2. Persist + validate + link via workflow.start.
   305	    from backend import workflow as wf
   306	    metadata = dict(req.metadata or {})
   307	    metadata.setdefault("source", "api:dag-submit")
   308	    metadata.setdefault("user", getattr(_user, "email", "operator"))
   309	
   310	    # Phase 64-C-LOCAL S4: resolve target_platform once and thread it
   311	    # through so wf.start's internal validator + downstream dispatcher
   312	    # get the same answer. Stash the profile name in metadata for
   313	    # post-hoc debugging of "why did this plan validate / not validate".
   314	    target_profile = _resolve_target_profile(req.target_platform)
   315	    if target_profile is not None:
   316	        metadata.setdefault(
   317	            "target_platform", target_profile.get("platform") or req.target_platform or "host_native",
   318	        )
   319	
   320	    # First attempt — workflow.start itself runs the validator.
   321	    run = await wf.start("invoke", dag=dag, metadata=metadata, target_profile=target_profile)
   322	    plan = await _ds.get_plan_by_run(run.id)
   323	    if plan is None:
   324	        # Plan persistence failed inside workflow.start — return best-
   325	        # effort so the caller can retry.
   326	        return JSONResponse(
   327	            status_code=500,
   328	            content={"detail": "plan persistence failed",
   329	                     "run_id": run.id},
   330	        )
   331	
   332	    # 3. If the plan failed validation AND caller opted into mutate,
   333	    #    kick the Orchestrator loop.
   334	    if plan.status == "failed" and req.mutate:
   335	        from backend import dag_planner as dp
   336	        # Before we attempt to mutate, drop any pre-warms that were
   337	        # speculatively launched against the prior draft — the
   338	        # replanned DAG will have different in-degree-0 tasks.
   339	        await _cancel_prewarm(reason="dag_mutated")
   340	        loop = await dp.run_mutation_loop(dag, ask_fn=_default_ask_fn)
   341	        if loop.ok:
   342	            # Open a successor run with the recovered DAG.
   343	            successor = await wf.mutate_workflow(
   344	                run.id, loop.final_dag, mutation_round=1,
   345	            )
   346	            succ_plan = await _ds.get_plan_by_run(successor.id)
   347	            return {
   348	                "run_id": successor.id,
   349	                "plan_id": succ_plan.id if succ_plan else None,
   350	                "status": succ_plan.status if succ_plan else "unknown",
   351	                "mutation_rounds": len(loop.attempts),
   352	                "supersedes_run_id": run.id,
   353	                "validation_errors": [],
   354	            }
   355	        # Exhausted — return the failed plan as-is; DE `dag/exhausted`
   356	        # proposal already fired inside run_mutation_loop.
   357	        return JSONResponse(
   358	            status_code=422,
   359	            content={
   360	                "run_id": run.id,
   361	                "plan_id": plan.id,
   362	                "status": plan.status,
   363	                "mutation_rounds": len(loop.attempts),
   364	                "mutation_status": loop.status,
   365	                "validation_errors": plan.errors(),
   366	                "stage": "mutation_exhausted",
   367	            },
   368	        )
   369	
   370	    # 4. Normal path — plain submit, no mutation. Return whatever
   371	    #    status we landed at (validated / executing / failed).
   372	    status_code = 200 if plan.status != "failed" else 422
   373	
   374	    # Phase 67-C hook: only fire pre-warm on validated plans AND when
   375	    # opt-in. We fire-and-forget with asyncio.create_task so the
   376	    # response returns immediately; pre-warm continues in background.
   377	    if plan.status == "executing" and _prewarm_enabled():
   378	        import asyncio as _asyncio
   379	        _asyncio.create_task(_prewarm_in_background(dag))

   521	            self._client = get_sync_redis()
   522	        if self._client is None:
   523	            raise RuntimeError(
   524	                "RedisHeartbeatStore requires OMNISIGHT_REDIS_URL"
   525	            )
   526	
   527	    def _alive_key(self, wid: str) -> str:
   528	        return f"{WORKER_HEARTBEAT_PREFIX}{wid}:alive"
   529	
   530	    def _set_key(self) -> str:
   531	        return f"{WORKER_HEARTBEAT_PREFIX}active"
   532	
   533	    def register(self, worker_id: str, info: dict[str, Any],
   534	                 ttl_s: int) -> None:
   535	        payload = json.dumps(info, sort_keys=True, default=str)
   536	        pipe = self._client.pipeline()
   537	        pipe.set(self._alive_key(worker_id), payload, ex=ttl_s)
   538	        pipe.sadd(self._set_key(), worker_id)
   539	        pipe.execute()
   540	
   541	    def heartbeat(self, worker_id: str, info: dict[str, Any],
   542	                  ttl_s: int) -> bool:
   543	        payload = json.dumps(info, sort_keys=True, default=str)
   544	        return bool(self._client.set(
   545	            self._alive_key(worker_id), payload, ex=ttl_s,
   546	        ))
   547	
   548	    def deregister(self, worker_id: str) -> None:
   549	        pipe = self._client.pipeline()
   550	        pipe.delete(self._alive_key(worker_id))
   551	        pipe.srem(self._set_key(), worker_id)
   552	        pipe.execute()
   553	
   554	    def list_active(self) -> list[str]:
   555	        members = self._client.smembers(self._set_key()) or set()
   556	        live: list[str] = []
   557	        for m in members:
   558	            wid = m.decode() if isinstance(m, bytes) else m
   559	            if self._client.exists(self._alive_key(wid)):
   560	                live.append(wid)
   561	            else:
   562	                # Stale registry entry — drop it.
   563	                self._client.srem(self._set_key(), wid)
   564	        return sorted(live)
   565	
   566	    def get_info(self, worker_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   567	        raw = self._client.get(self._alive_key(worker_id))
   568	        if not raw:
   569	            return None
   570	        if isinstance(raw, bytes):
   571	            raw = raw.decode()
   572	        try:
   573	            return json.loads(raw)
   574	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   575	            return None

   621	
   622	def _resolve_glob(root: Path, glob: str) -> list[Path]:
   623	    """Resolve a CATC ``impact_scope.allowed`` glob into existing paths.
   624	
   625	    Honours the project-root jail: any path resolving outside ``root``
   626	    is rejected (and the worker will refuse the task) — this is the
   627	    "physically unreachable" guarantee in the spec.
   628	    """
   629	    glob = glob.lstrip("/")
   630	    if not glob:
   631	        return []
   632	    # Reject ".." segments before letting Python expand the glob.
   633	    if any(part == ".." for part in Path(glob).parts):
   634	        raise ValueError(
   635	            f"impact_scope.allowed glob escapes project root: {glob!r}"
   636	        )
   637	    matches: list[Path] = []
   638	    for raw in root.glob(glob):
   639	        try:
   640	            raw_resolved = raw.resolve()
   641	            root_resolved = root.resolve()
   642	            raw_resolved.relative_to(root_resolved)
   643	        except (ValueError, OSError):
   644	            raise ValueError(
   645	                f"impact_scope.allowed glob escapes project root: {glob!r}"
   646	            )
   647	        matches.append(raw)
   648	    if not matches:
   649	        # If the literal path doesn't exist yet (e.g. the agent will
   650	        # create it), still allow the worker to proceed by recording
   651	        # an empty match — the workspace will be empty until commit.
   652	        return []
   653	    return matches
   654	
   655	
   656	def _run_git(cwd: Path, args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
   657	    import subprocess
   658	    proc = subprocess.run(
   659	        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True,
   660	    )
   661	    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr

   665	#  Worker
   666	# ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   671	    return f"{prefix}-{host}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"

   673	
   674	class Worker:
   675	    """One stateless worker process.
   676	
   677	    Lifecycle::
   678	
   679	        w = Worker(config, sandbox_runtime, agent_executor, gerrit_pusher)
   680	        w.start()       # registers, starts heartbeat thread
   681	        try:
   682	            w.run()     # blocks pulling + processing tasks
   683	        finally:
   684	            w.stop()    # graceful: stop claiming, finish in-flight,
   685	                        # release locks, deregister
   686	    """
   687	
   688	    def __init__(self,
   689	                 config: WorkerConfig,
   690	                 *,
   691	                 sandbox_runtime: SandboxRuntime | None = None,
   692	                 agent_executor: AgentExecutor | None = None,
   693	                 gerrit_pusher: GerritPusher | None = None,
   694	                 heartbeat_store: HeartbeatStore | None = None,
   695	                 ) -> None:
   696	        self.config = config
   697	        self.sandbox = sandbox_runtime or LocalSandboxRuntime()
   698	        self.executor = agent_executor or _StubAgentExecutor()
   699	        self.gerrit = gerrit_pusher or StubGerritPusher()
   700	        self.store = heartbeat_store or _get_default_store()
   701	
   702	        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
   703	        self._heartbeat_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
   704	        self._inflight: dict[str, str] = {}        # message_id -> task_id
   705	        self._inflight_lock = threading.Lock()
   706	        self._pending = 0                          # submitted-but-not-started
   707	        self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
   708	        self._processed: list[WorkerTaskOutcome] = []
   709	        self._processed_lock = threading.Lock()
   710	        self._executor_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = None
   711	        self._started_at: float = 0.0
   712	        self._signal_handlers_installed = False
   713	
   714	    # ─── lifecycle ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   715	
   716	    def start(self) -> None:
   717	        self._started_at = time.time()
   718	        info = self._info_snapshot(status="starting")
   719	        self.store.register(self.config.worker_id, info,
   720	                            self.config.heartbeat_ttl_s)
   721	        _bump_workers_active(self.store)
   722	        self._executor_pool = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
   723	            max_workers=max(1, self.config.capacity),
   724	            thread_name_prefix=f"wkr-{self.config.worker_id}",
   725	        )
   726	        self._heartbeat_thread = threading.Thread(
   727	            target=self._heartbeat_loop,
   728	            name=f"worker-heartbeat-{self.config.worker_id}",
   729	            daemon=True,
   730	        )
   731	        self._heartbeat_thread.start()
   732	        logger.info(
   733	            "worker %s started (capacity=%d, tenant_filter=%s, "
   734	            "capability_filter=%s)",
   735	            self.config.worker_id, self.config.capacity,
   736	            self.config.tenant_filter or "*",
   737	            self.config.capability_filter or "*",
   738	        )
   739	        try:
   740	            metrics.worker_lifecycle_total.labels(event="start").inc()
   741	        except Exception:
   742	            pass
   743	
   744	    def stop(self, *, timeout_s: float = 60.0) -> None:
   745	        """Graceful shutdown.
   746	
   747	        After this returns, ``stop_event`` is set, the heartbeat
   748	        thread has exited, no in-flight task is still claimed, and
   749	        the worker is deregistered from the active set.
   750	        """
   751	        if self._stop_event.is_set():
   752	            return
   753	        self._stop_event.set()
   754	        # Wait for in-flight + pending tasks to drain (run() loop does the work).
   755	        deadline = time.time() + timeout_s
   756	        while True:
   757	            with self._inflight_lock:
   758	                inflight = len(self._inflight)
   759	            pending = self._pending_count()
   760	            if inflight == 0 and pending == 0:
   760	            if inflight == 0 and pending == 0:
   761	                break
   762	            if time.time() >= deadline:
   763	                logger.warning(
   764	                    "worker %s stop: %d in-flight task(s) still running "
   765	                    "after %.1fs — abandoning",
   766	                    self.config.worker_id, len(self._inflight), timeout_s,
   767	                )
   768	                # Best-effort: nack each in-flight to release the
   769	                # visibility timeout faster + release any locks.
   770	                with self._inflight_lock:
   771	                    in_flight = dict(self._inflight)
   772	                for mid, tid in in_flight.items():
   773	                    self._abandon(mid, tid, "worker stop timeout")
   774	                break
   775	            time.sleep(0.05)
   776	
   777	        if self._executor_pool is not None:
   778	            # We've already drained in-flight tasks above; this is just
   779	            # to release the pool's worker threads.
   780	            self._executor_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False)
   781	            self._executor_pool = None
   782	        if self._heartbeat_thread is not None:
   783	            self._heartbeat_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
   784	        try:
   785	            self.store.deregister(self.config.worker_id)
   786	        except Exception as exc:
   787	            logger.warning("worker %s deregister failed: %s",
   788	                           self.config.worker_id, exc)
   789	        _bump_workers_active(self.store)
   790	        try:
   791	            metrics.worker_lifecycle_total.labels(event="stop").inc()
   792	        except Exception:
   793	            pass
   794	        logger.info("worker %s stopped (processed=%d)",
   795	                    self.config.worker_id, len(self._processed))
   796	
   797	    def install_signal_handlers(self) -> None:
   798	        """Wire SIGTERM / SIGINT to ``stop()`` for systemd / docker."""
   799	        if self._signal_handlers_installed:
   800	            return
   801	        if threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread():
   802	            # signal.signal must be called from main thread.
   803	            return
   804	
   805	        def _handler(signum: int, _frame: Any) -> None:
   806	            logger.info("worker %s caught signal %d — graceful shutdown",
   807	                        self.config.worker_id, signum)
   808	            self._stop_event.set()
   809	
   810	        for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
   811	            try:
   812	                signal.signal(sig, _handler)
   813	            except (ValueError, OSError):
   814	                # In some embedded runtimes setting signals raises.
   815	                pass
   816	        self._signal_handlers_installed = True
   817	
   818	    # ─── main loop ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   819	
   820	    def run(self) -> list[WorkerTaskOutcome]:
   821	        """Block pulling + processing tasks until ``stop_event`` set
   822	        or ``max_messages`` reached.
   823	
   824	        Returns the per-task outcome list — useful for tests + for
   825	        the systemd ExecStop hook to log a summary.
   826	        """
   827	        n = 0
   828	        while not self._stop_event.is_set():
   829	            if (self.config.max_messages is not None
   830	                    and n >= self.config.max_messages):
   831	                break
   832	            free = self.config.capacity - max(
   833	                self._inflight_count(), self._pending_count(),
   834	            )
   835	            if free <= 0:
   836	                time.sleep(self.config.loop_idle_s)
   837	                continue
   838	            pull_n = min(self.config.effective_pull_count(), free)
   839	            try:
   840	                msgs = queue_backend.pull(
   841	                    self.config.worker_id, count=pull_n,
   842	                    visibility_timeout_s=self.config.visibility_timeout_s,
   843	                )
   844	            except Exception as exc:
   845	                logger.exception("worker %s pull failed: %s",
   846	                                 self.config.worker_id, exc)
   847	                time.sleep(self.config.loop_idle_s)
   848	                continue
   849	
   850	            if not msgs:
   851	                time.sleep(self.config.loop_idle_s)
   852	                continue
   853	
   854	            for msg in msgs:
   855	                if self._stop_event.is_set():
   856	                    # Re-queue immediately by returning the message
   857	                    # to Queued; visibility timeout would do this
   858	                    # eventually but we want the next worker to take
   859	                    # it now (graceful shutdown spec).
   860	                    self._return_to_queue(msg, "worker shutting down")
   861	                    self._record_outcome(self._filter_outcome(
   862	                        msg, "shutdown_returned",
   863	                        "worker shutting down",
   864	                    ))
   865	                    n += 1
   866	                    continue
   867	                if not self._matches_filters(msg):
   868	                    self._return_to_queue(
   869	                        msg, "filter mismatch (tenant/capability)",
   870	                    )
   871	                    self._record_outcome(self._filter_outcome(
   872	                        msg, "nacked",
   873	                        "filter mismatch (tenant/capability)",
   874	                    ))
   875	                    n += 1
   876	                    continue
   877	                # Dispatch into the thread pool so the worker can have
   878	                # up to ``capacity`` tasks in-flight at once (spec:
   879	                # ``--capacity N``).  ``handle()`` never raises so we
   880	                # don't bother chaining a future callback.
   881	                if self.config.capacity == 1 or self._executor_pool is None:
   882	                    self._record_outcome(self.handle(msg))
   883	                else:
   884	                    with self._pending_lock:
   885	                        self._pending += 1
   886	                    self._executor_pool.submit(
   887	                        self._handle_and_record, msg,
   888	                    )
   889	                n += 1
   890	
   891	        # Wait for any remaining submitted tasks (capacity > 1 case).
   892	        # ``_pending`` is bumped at submit() and decremented in
   893	        # ``_handle_and_record`` AFTER the outcome is appended, so
   894	        # waiting on it == waiting for every outcome to be in
   895	        # ``self._processed``.
   896	        if self._executor_pool is not None:
   897	            deadline = time.time() + 60.0
   898	            while self._pending_count() > 0 and time.time() < deadline:
   899	                time.sleep(0.02)
   900	        return list(self._processed)
   901	
   902	    def _handle_and_record(self, msg: QueueMessage) -> None:
   903	        try:
   904	            self._record_outcome(self.handle(msg))
   905	        except Exception as exc:                       # pragma: no cover
   906	            logger.exception("handle(%s) crashed: %s", msg.message_id, exc)
   907	        finally:
   908	            with self._pending_lock:
   909	                self._pending -= 1
   910	
   911	    def _pending_count(self) -> int:
   912	        with self._pending_lock:
   913	            return self._pending
   914	
   915	    def _record_outcome(self, outcome: WorkerTaskOutcome) -> None:
   916	        with self._processed_lock:
   917	            self._processed.append(outcome)
   918	
   919	    # ─── single-task processing ──────────────────────────────────
   920	
   921	    def handle(self, msg: QueueMessage) -> WorkerTaskOutcome:
   922	        """Process one ``QueueMessage`` end-to-end.
   923	
   924	        Returns a ``WorkerTaskOutcome`` audit row.  Never raises:
   925	        every failure path is caught and translated into ``nack``
   926	        (queue handles 3-strike + DLQ) so the worker loop can keep
   927	        going.
   928	        """
   929	        started = time.time()
   930	        task_id = _task_id_for(msg)
   931	        outcome = WorkerTaskOutcome(
   932	            message_id=msg.message_id,
   933	            task_id=task_id,
   934	            jira_ticket=_safe_ticket(msg),
   935	            status="acked",
   936	        )
   937	        # O10 (#273): reject forged / tampered queue payloads *before*
   938	        # touching the sandbox.  When no HMAC key is configured the call
   939	        # is a no-op and we fall back to pre-O10 behaviour.
   940	        try:
   941	            queue_backend.verify_pulled_message(msg)
   942	        except Exception as exc:
   943	            outcome.status = "nacked"
   944	            outcome.error = f"O10 HMAC verify failed: {exc}"
   945	            # Immediate DLQ — a bad signature is not a transient fault and
   946	            # re-queueing it would just poison the next puller.  We NACK
   947	            # MAX_DELIVERIES times to trigger DLQ in one call.
   948	            try:
   949	                for _ in range(queue_backend.MAX_DELIVERIES):
   950	                    queue_backend.nack(
   951	                        msg.message_id, outcome.error,
   952	                        queue_backend.format_exc(exc),
   953	                    )
   954	            except Exception:
   955	                pass
   956	            outcome.elapsed_s = time.time() - started
   957	            try:
   958	                metrics.worker_task_total.labels(outcome="hmac_rejected").inc()
   959	            except Exception:
   960	                pass
   961	            return outcome
   962	        try:
   963	            card = msg.task_card()
   964	        except Exception as exc:
   965	            outcome.status = "nacked"
   966	            outcome.error = f"corrupt CATC payload: {exc}"
   967	            queue_backend.nack(msg.message_id,
   968	                               outcome.error,
   969	                               queue_backend.format_exc(exc))
   970	            outcome.elapsed_s = time.time() - started
   971	            return outcome
   972	
   973	        # ─── distributed lock on impact_scope.allowed ───────────
   974	        allowed_paths = list(card.navigation.impact_scope.allowed)
   975	        lock_res = dist_lock.acquire_paths(
   976	            task_id, allowed_paths, ttl_s=self.config.lock_ttl_s,
   977	            wait_timeout_s=self.config.lock_wait_s,
   978	        )
   979	        if not lock_res.ok:
   980	            outcome.status = "locked_skipped"

  1104	    # ─── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1105	
  1106	    def _matches_filters(self, msg: QueueMessage) -> bool:
  1107	        if not self.config.tenant_filter and not self.config.capability_filter:
  1108	            return True
  1109	        tenant = _msg_tenant(msg)
  1110	        if self.config.tenant_filter and tenant not in self.config.tenant_filter:
  1111	            return False
  1112	        if self.config.capability_filter:
  1113	            caps = _msg_capabilities(msg)
  1114	            if not any(c in self.config.capability_filter for c in caps):
  1115	                return False
  1116	        return True
  1117	
  1118	    def _filter_outcome(self, msg: QueueMessage, status: str,
  1119	                        reason: str) -> WorkerTaskOutcome:
  1120	        return WorkerTaskOutcome(
  1121	            message_id=msg.message_id,
  1122	            task_id=_task_id_for(msg),
  1123	            jira_ticket=_safe_ticket(msg),
  1124	            status=status,
  1125	            error=reason,
  1126	        )
  1127	
  1128	    def _return_to_queue(self, msg: QueueMessage, reason: str) -> None:
  1129	        """Best-effort: bump delivery_count back without consuming a
  1130	        retry budget by re-queueing via state transition.
  1131	
  1132	        We can't truly "un-claim" a message in O2's contract — but the
  1133	        next ``sweep_visibility`` will do it for us once the deadline
  1134	        passes.  For graceful shutdown / filter mismatch we still
  1135	        prefer to nack with a benign reason so the queue can re-deliver
  1135	        prefer to nack with a benign reason so the queue can re-deliver
  1136	        immediately, AT THE COST of one delivery_count tick.  3-strike
  1137	        rule applies — operators shouldn't loop a worker between
  1138	        filters that always reject.
  1139	        """
  1140	        try:
  1141	            queue_backend.nack(msg.message_id, reason)
  1142	        except Exception as exc:
  1143	            logger.warning("return_to_queue(%s) failed: %s",
  1144	                           msg.message_id, exc)
  1145	
  1146	    def _abandon(self, message_id: str, task_id: str, reason: str) -> None:
  1147	        try:
  1148	            queue_backend.nack(message_id, reason)
  1149	        except Exception:
  1150	            pass
  1151	        try:
  1152	            dist_lock.release_paths(task_id)
  1153	        except Exception:
  1154	            pass
  1155	
  1156	    def _track_inflight(self, message_id: str, task_id: str) -> None:
  1157	        with self._inflight_lock:
  1158	            self._inflight[message_id] = task_id
  1159	        try:
  1160	            metrics.worker_inflight.set(self._inflight_count())
  1161	        except Exception:
  1162	            pass
  1163	
  1164	    def _untrack_inflight(self, message_id: str) -> None:
  1165	        with self._inflight_lock:
  1166	            self._inflight.pop(message_id, None)
  1167	        try:
  1168	            metrics.worker_inflight.set(self._inflight_count())
  1169	        except Exception:
  1170	            pass
  1171	
  1172	    def _inflight_count(self) -> int:
  1173	        with self._inflight_lock:
  1174	            return len(self._inflight)
  1175	
  1176	    def _heartbeat_loop(self) -> None:
  1177	        while not self._stop_event.wait(self.config.heartbeat_interval_s):
  1178	            try:
  1179	                self.store.heartbeat(
  1180	                    self.config.worker_id,
  1181	                    self._info_snapshot(status="alive"),
  1182	                    self.config.heartbeat_ttl_s,
  1183	                )
  1184	                try:
  1185	                    metrics.worker_heartbeat_total.inc()
  1186	                except Exception:
  1187	                    pass
  1188	            except Exception as exc:
  1189	                logger.warning(
  1190	                    "worker %s heartbeat failed: %s",
  1191	                    self.config.worker_id, exc,
  1192	                )
  1193	
  1194	    def _info_snapshot(self, *, status: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
  1195	        snap = {
  1196	            "worker_id": self.config.worker_id,
  1197	            "host": socket.gethostname(),
  1198	            "pid": os.getpid(),
  1199	            "status": status,
  1200	            "capacity": self.config.capacity,
  1201	            "tenant_filter": list(self.config.tenant_filter),
  1202	            "capability_filter": list(self.config.capability_filter),
  1203	            "started_at": self._started_at,
  1204	            "inflight": self._inflight_count(),
  1205	            "processed": len(self._processed),
  1206	        }
  1207	        # O10 (#273): advertise the TLS certificate fingerprint so the
  1208	        # orchestrator / dashboard can pin it — if the cert rotates
  1209	        # without an ops approval, the next attestation will fail.
  1210	        fp = os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_WORKER_TLS_FP", "").strip()
  1211	        if fp:
  1212	            snap["tls_cert_fingerprint"] = fp
  1213	        return snap

   302	def _derive_allowed_globs(task: Task) -> list[str]:
   303	    """Derive a conservative ``impact_scope.allowed`` glob set from a
   304	    DAG task.  Prefers the task's own ``expected_output`` when it looks
   305	    like a file path; expands the directory so the worker can touch
   306	    siblings on that component.  Falls back to a single literal path
   307	    when only the exact file should be mutable.
   308	
   309	    We purposely do NOT include upstream-task outputs here — those are
   310	    reads, not writes, and the CATC contract says ``allowed`` is the
   311	    write scope.
   312	    """
   313	    out = task.expected_output.strip()
   314	    if _FILE_PATH_HINT.match(out):
   315	        # Widen to the directory — a real task typically touches more
   316	        # than one file within the same module.
   317	        parent = out.rsplit("/", 1)[0] if "/" in out else ""
   318	        if parent:
   319	            return [f"{parent}/**"]
   320	        return [out]
   321	    # Non-file outputs (git:<sha>, issue:<id>) — fall back to task_id-
   322	    # derived scratch directory.  Worker is responsible for respecting it.
   323	    slug = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.\-]", "_", task.task_id)
   324	    return [f"artifacts/{slug}/**"]

   327	def _subtask_key(jira_ticket: str, index: int) -> str:
   328	    """Construct a deterministic JIRA-style subtask key.  Kept inside
   329	    the 64-char CATC limit and matches ``[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-\\d+`` so the
   330	    downstream CATC validator accepts it."""
   331	    m = re.match(r"^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)-(\d+)$", jira_ticket)
   332	    if not m:
   333	        # Defensive — caller should have rejected at intake_from_webhook
   334	        return f"{jira_ticket}-{index + 1}"
   335	    prefix, base = m.group(1), m.group(2)
   336	    return f"{prefix}-{int(base) * 1000 + index + 1}"

   339	def build_catcs_from_dag(jira_ticket: str, dag: DAG,
   340	                         *, acceptance_criteria: str = "",
   341	                         domain_context: str = "",
   342	                         size: str = "M",
   343	                         forbidden_globs: list[str] | None = None,
   344	                         ) -> list[TaskCard]:
   345	    """Produce one TaskCard per DAG node.
   346	
   347	    ``forbidden_globs`` (optional) is applied wholesale to every card
   348	    — useful when the operator wants the entire intake walled off from
   349	    e.g. ``test_assets/**`` (read-only ground truth per CLAUDE.md L1).
   350	    """
   351	    forbidden = list(forbidden_globs or [])
   352	    cards: list[TaskCard] = []
   353	    for i, task in enumerate(dag.tasks):
   354	        allowed = _derive_allowed_globs(task)
   355	        ac = acceptance_criteria.strip() or task.description
   356	        card = TaskCard.from_dict({
   357	            "jira_ticket": _subtask_key(jira_ticket, i),
   358	            "acceptance_criteria": ac,
   359	            "navigation": {
   360	                "entry_point": task.expected_output if _FILE_PATH_HINT.match(
   361	                    task.expected_output) else f"#{task.task_id}",
   362	                "impact_scope": {
   363	                    "allowed": allowed,
   364	                    "forbidden": forbidden,
   365	                },
   366	            },
   367	            "domain_context": (
   368	                domain_context or f"topology_size={size} task={task.task_id}"
   369	            ),
   370	            "handoff_protocol": [
   371	                f"topology_size:{size}",
   372	                f"Run toolchain: {task.toolchain}",
   373	                "Commit changes and push to Gerrit refs/for/main",
   374	            ],
   375	        })
   376	        cards.append(card)
   377	    return cards

   385	@dataclass
   386	class ScopeConflict:
   387	    card_a_index: int
   388	    card_b_index: int
   389	    a_task_id: str
   390	    b_task_id: str
   391	    overlap: tuple[str, str]    # the two globs that conflicted
   392	
   393	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   394	        return {
   395	            "card_a": self.a_task_id,
   396	            "card_b": self.b_task_id,
   397	            "glob_a": self.overlap[0],
   398	            "glob_b": self.overlap[1],
   399	        }

   401	
   402	def check_impact_scope_intersect(cards: list[TaskCard], dag: DAG | None = None,
   403	                                 ) -> list[ScopeConflict]:
   404	    """Return all pairwise ``allowed`` glob overlaps.
   405	
   406	    Two CATC cards in the same sprint may both legitimately touch the
   407	    same scope ONLY if one depends on the other (serial execution is
   408	    fine — they can't conflict at runtime because the dist-lock
   409	    serialises them).  If ``dag`` is supplied, we skip pairs that are
   410	    transitively connected in the dependency graph; otherwise every
   411	    overlap is reported.
   412	    """
   413	    # Pre-compute dep closure when a DAG is available.
   414	    connected: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
   415	    if dag is not None:
   416	        # Build adjacency (forward + reverse) and BFS both directions
   417	        # to flatten ancestor+descendant into one "serial"-ness set.
   418	        children: dict[str, list[str]] = {t.task_id: [] for t in dag.tasks}
   419	        parents: dict[str, list[str]] = {t.task_id: list(t.depends_on)
   420	                                         for t in dag.tasks}
   421	        for t in dag.tasks:
   422	            for dep in t.depends_on:
   423	                children.setdefault(dep, []).append(t.task_id)
   424	
   425	        def _reachable(start: str, adj: dict[str, list[str]]) -> set[str]:
   426	            seen: set[str] = set()
   427	            stack = list(adj.get(start, []))
   428	            while stack:
   429	                n = stack.pop()
   430	                if n in seen:
   430	                if n in seen:
   431	                    continue
   432	                seen.add(n)
   433	                stack.extend(adj.get(n, []))
   434	            return seen
   435	
   436	        for t in dag.tasks:
   437	            for d in _reachable(t.task_id, children):
   438	                connected.add((t.task_id, d))
   439	                connected.add((d, t.task_id))
   440	            for a in _reachable(t.task_id, parents):
   441	                connected.add((t.task_id, a))
   442	                connected.add((a, t.task_id))
   443	
   444	    conflicts: list[ScopeConflict] = []
   445	    # We pull the task_id from the DAG by index (cards were built in
   446	    # DAG order by ``build_catcs_from_dag``).
   447	    task_ids = [t.task_id for t in (dag.tasks if dag else [])]
   448	    if not task_ids or len(task_ids) != len(cards):
   449	        task_ids = [c.jira_ticket for c in cards]
   450	
   451	    for i in range(len(cards)):
   452	        a = cards[i]
   453	        ai = task_ids[i]
   454	        for j in range(i + 1, len(cards)):
   455	            b = cards[j]
   456	            bi = task_ids[j]
   457	            if (ai, bi) in connected:
   458	                continue
   459	            overlap = _first_glob_overlap(
   460	                a.navigation.impact_scope.allowed,
   461	                b.navigation.impact_scope.allowed,
   462	            )
   463	            if overlap is None:
   464	                continue
   465	            conflicts.append(ScopeConflict(
   466	                card_a_index=i, card_b_index=j,
   467	                a_task_id=ai, b_task_id=bi,
   468	                overlap=overlap,
   469	            ))
   470	    return conflicts
   471	
   472	
   473	def _first_glob_overlap(left: list[str], right: list[str]
   474	                        ) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
   475	    for g1 in left:
   476	        for g2 in right:
   477	            if globs_overlap(g1, g2):
   478	                return (g1, g2)
   479	    return None

   483	#  Complexity scoring
   484	# ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   486	
   487	def complexity_score(dag: DAG) -> int:
   488	    """Back-of-envelope DAG complexity score.
   489	
   490	    Combines node count, edge count, and max fan-in/out so that a
   491	    pathologically deep or branched plan trips ``require_human_review``
   492	    even when it stays under the 10-task "simple" bucket.
   493	
   494	    Score breakdown:
   495	      * 2 × len(tasks)
   496	      * 1 × len(edges)
   497	      * 3 × max(fan_in, fan_out)
   498	      * +5 if any task sits on a path of length ≥ 4
   499	    """
   500	    n = len(dag.tasks)
   501	    edges = 0
   502	    fan_in: dict[str, int] = {t.task_id: 0 for t in dag.tasks}
   503	    fan_out: dict[str, int] = {t.task_id: 0 for t in dag.tasks}
   504	    for t in dag.tasks:
   505	        edges += len(t.depends_on)
   506	        fan_out[t.task_id] = len(t.depends_on)  # reversed below? see note
   507	    # We want "fan_in" = how many tasks depend ON t; "fan_out" = how
   508	    # many deps t itself has.  Re-compute fan_in by scanning depends_on.
   509	    fan_in = {t.task_id: 0 for t in dag.tasks}
   510	    for t in dag.tasks:
   511	        for d in t.depends_on:
   512	            if d in fan_in:
   513	                fan_in[d] += 1
   514	    max_fan = max([*fan_in.values(), *fan_out.values(), 0])
   515	
   516	    # Depth via simple topological longest-path.
   517	    adj: dict[str, list[str]] = {t.task_id: [] for t in dag.tasks}
   518	    for t in dag.tasks:
   519	        for d in t.depends_on:
   520	            adj.setdefault(d, []).append(t.task_id)
   521	
   522	    depth_by_id: dict[str, int] = {}
   523	
   524	    def _depth(node: str, stack: set[str]) -> int:
   525	        if node in depth_by_id:
   526	            return depth_by_id[node]
   527	        if node in stack:
   528	            return 0    # cycle — validator will reject later
   529	        stack.add(node)
   530	        best = 0
   531	        for nxt in adj.get(node, []):
   532	            best = max(best, 1 + _depth(nxt, stack))
   533	        stack.discard(node)
   534	        depth_by_id[node] = best
   535	        return best
   536	
   537	    deepest = 0
   538	    for t in dag.tasks:
   539	        deepest = max(deepest, _depth(t.task_id, set()))
   540	
   541	    score = 2 * n + edges + 3 * max_fan + (5 if deepest >= 4 else 0)
   542	    return int(score)
   543

   903	async def start_t3_local_container(agent_id: str, workspace_path: Path,
   904	                                   *, tenant_id: str | None = None,
   905	                                   tenant_budget: float | None = None) -> ContainerInfo:
   906	    """Phase 64-C-LOCAL S2 — T3 executor for the host==target path.
   907	
   908	    Used by the T3 runner when `t3_resolver.resolve_t3_runner()` has
   909	    picked the LOCAL kind: same arch, same OS, so a binary built in
   910	    this sandbox can run on the host. Concretely, `--network host`
   911	    so smoke-tests against localhost / systemd-managed services work,
   912	    plus the same runsc/workspace envelope T1 ships with.
   913	
   914	    Callers should go through `t3_resolver.resolve_t3_runner()` rather
   915	    than invoking this directly — it records the metric and delegates.
   916	
   917	    Deploy actions that need to mutate host state (systemctl enable,
   918	    write to /etc/nginx/, etc.) should still NOT happen inside this
   919	    container. The pattern is: agent produces artefact + install.sh
   920	    in /workspace, orchestrator runs install.sh on the host (outside
   921	    the sandbox) as a separate pipeline step. That keeps the sandbox
   922	    a containment boundary even on the happy-path.
   923	    """
   924	    return await start_container(
   925	        agent_id, workspace_path, tier="t3-local",
   926	        tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_budget=tenant_budget,
   927	    )

   929	
   930	async def dispatch_t3(
   931	    agent_id: str,
   932	    workspace_path: Path,
   933	    target_arch: str = "",
   934	    target_os: str = "linux",
   935	    *,
   936	    tenant_id: str | None = None,
   937	    tenant_budget: float | None = None,
   938	) -> "tuple[ContainerInfo | None, T3RunnerKind]":  # noqa: F821
   939	    """Phase 64-C-LOCAL S2 — single entry point for the T3 dispatcher.
   940	
   941	    Consults the resolver, bumps the prometheus counter so the Ops
   942	    Summary panel (S4) can show a live runner distribution, and
   943	    returns (ContainerInfo, RunnerKind). Returns (None, BUNDLE) when
   944	    no live runner is available yet — caller is expected to fall
   945	    back to the artefact-bundle path.
   946	
   947	    Extending to SSH/QEMU is additive in this function: as each kind
   948	    gains a backing runner, add a branch here; call sites don't change.
   949	    """
   950	    from backend.t3_resolver import (
   951	        T3RunnerKind, record_dispatch, resolve_t3_runner,
   952	    )
   953	    res = resolve_t3_runner(target_arch, target_os)
   954	    record_dispatch(res.kind)
   955	    logger.info(
   956	        "dispatch_t3: agent=%s target=%s/%s → %s (%s)",
   957	        agent_id, res.target_arch or "?", res.target_os,
   958	        res.kind.value, res.reason,
   959	    )
   960	    if res.kind == T3RunnerKind.LOCAL:
   961	        info = await start_t3_local_container(
   962	            agent_id, workspace_path,
   963	            tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_budget=tenant_budget,
   964	        )
   965	        return info, res.kind
   966	    if res.kind == T3RunnerKind.SSH:
   967	        from backend.ssh_runner import find_target_for_arch, SSHRunnerInfo
   968	        ssh_target = find_target_for_arch(res.target_arch, res.target_os)
   969	        if ssh_target is not None:
   970	            ssh_info = SSHRunnerInfo(
   971	                agent_id=agent_id,
   972	                target=ssh_target,
   973	                status="ready",
   974	            )
   975	            return ssh_info, res.kind
   976	        logger.warning(
   977	            "dispatch_t3: resolver said SSH but no target found for %s/%s",
   978	            res.target_arch, res.target_os,
   979	        )
   980	        return None, T3RunnerKind.BUNDLE
   981	    # BUNDLE / QEMU (64-C-QEMU): no live runner yet; caller handles
   982	    # the bundling / remote dispatch at the orchestrator layer.
   983	    return None, res.kind

   986	async def exec_in_container(
   987	    container_id_or_name: str,
   988	    command: str,
   989	    timeout: int = DOCKER_TIMEOUT,
   990	    *,
   991	    tier: str = "t1",
   992	) -> tuple[int, str]:
   993	    """Execute a command inside a running container.
   994	
   995	    Returns (exit_code, combined output). Output is hard-capped at
   996	    `OMNISIGHT_SANDBOX_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` (default 10 KB) to keep a
   997	    runaway command from blowing up the Tier-0 LLM context. Truncation
   998	    appends a one-line marker and bumps
   999	    `omnisight_sandbox_output_truncated_total{tier}`.
  1000	    """
  1001	    # C2 audit (2026-04-19): previous impl used bash -c "{command}" with
  1002	    # only a manual replace('"', '\\"') upstream in tools.py. That stops
  1003	    # literal double-quotes but lets `$(...)`, backticks, `$VAR`, and
  1004	    # newlines escape the outer-shell layer and execute BEFORE docker exec
  1005	    # sees the argument. shlex.quote single-quotes the whole command so
  1006	    # the outer /bin/sh sees it as one argv slot; `bash -c` inside the
  1007	    # container then unwraps the single-quoted literal.
  1008	    import shlex as _shlex
  1009	    rc, out, err = await _run(
  1010	        f'docker exec {container_id_or_name} bash -c {_shlex.quote(command)}',
  1011	        timeout=timeout,
  1012	    )
  1013	    combined = out
  1014	    if err:
  1015	        combined += f"\n[STDERR] {err}" if out else err
  1016	    # Phase 64-D D3: enforce per-exec output cap.
  1017	    from backend.config import settings as _settings
  1018	    cap = int(_settings.sandbox_max_output_bytes or 0)
  1019	    if cap > 0:
  1020	        b = combined.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
  1021	        if len(b) > cap:
  1022	            head = b[:cap].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
  1023	            combined = (
  1024	                f"{head}\n[TRUNCATED — {len(b)} bytes total, "
  1025	                f"cap={cap} via OMNISIGHT_SANDBOX_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES]"

     2	
     3	Historical T3 design assumed "a remote hardware daemon". That's fine
     4	for Jetson / Rockchip / MCU targets but overkill for the 90% use
     5	case: host == target (AMD 9950X WSL deploying to its own x86_64
     6	Linux). This module is the resolver layer that picks the right
     7	runner class based on arch/OS match + available capability.
     8	
     9	Hierarchy (top first; later SSH/QEMU land in follow-up phases):
    10	
    11	    required_tier=t3 → resolve_t3_runner(task, target_profile)
    12	      ├─ host_arch == target_arch && host_os == target_os → LOCAL  ⭐
    13	      ├─ registered_remote_runner_matches                  → SSH    (64-C-SSH)
    14	      ├─ can_qemu_emulate(target_arch)                     → QEMU   (64-C-QEMU)
    15	      └─ fallback                                          → BUNDLE (current)
    16	
    17	The resolver is consulted by:
    18	  * dag_validator — `tier_violation` rule passes when LOCAL (or any
    19	    live runner) can serve the task, fails otherwise.

    21	  * Ops Summary panel — shows per-runner dispatch counts.

    94	def native_arch_matches(target_arch: str, target_os: str = "linux") -> bool:
    95	    """Return True iff the host can natively execute the target's
    96	    binaries — same arch, same OS. Empty / unknown target arguments
    97	    intentionally return False: a missing target_arch must not be
    98	    silently treated as "matches host", or an under-specified DAG
    99	    would auto-route to LOCAL and hide its real target requirement.
   100	    """
   101	    if not target_arch or not target_os:
   102	        return False
   103	    return (
   104	        _canon_arch(target_arch) == host_arch()
   105	        and target_os.lower() == host_os()
   106	    )

   108	
   109	def resolve_t3_runner(
   110	    target_arch: str = "",
   111	    target_os: str = "linux",
   112	) -> T3Resolution:
   113	    """Pick a T3 runner for the given target. Single entry point —
   114	    both the validator (S3) and the executor (S2) go through here so
   115	    their decisions can't drift.
   116	
   117	    Order of preference: LOCAL → (SSH → QEMU in future phases) →
   118	    BUNDLE. Each candidate is checked in turn; the first that's
   119	    available wins.
   120	    """
   121	    h_arch = host_arch()
   122	    h_os = host_os()
   123	    t_arch = _canon_arch(target_arch) if target_arch else ""
   124	    t_os = (target_os or "linux").lower()
   125	
   126	    # 1. LOCAL — same arch, same OS, kill-switch not pulled.
   127	    if _local_enabled() and native_arch_matches(target_arch, target_os):
   128	        return T3Resolution(
   129	            kind=T3RunnerKind.LOCAL,
   130	            reason=f"host ({h_arch}/{h_os}) matches target ({t_arch}/{t_os})",
   131	            target_arch=t_arch, target_os=t_os,
   132	            host_arch=h_arch, host_os=h_os,
   133	        )
   134	
   135	    # 2. SSH — Phase 64-C-SSH. Check if a registered remote runner
   136	    #    matches the target arch.
   137	    if _ssh_enabled() and t_arch:
   138	        from backend.ssh_runner import find_target_for_arch
   139	        ssh_target = find_target_for_arch(t_arch, t_os)
   140	        if ssh_target is not None:
   141	            return T3Resolution(
   142	                kind=T3RunnerKind.SSH,
   143	                reason=(
   144	                    f"host ({h_arch}/{h_os}) ≠ target ({t_arch}/{t_os}); "
   145	                    f"SSH runner registered at {ssh_target.host}"
   146	                ),
   147	                target_arch=t_arch, target_os=t_os,
   148	                host_arch=h_arch, host_os=h_os,
   149	            )
   150	
   151	    # 3. QEMU — deferred (Phase 64-C-QEMU).
   152	
   153	    # 4. BUNDLE — current fallback: package artefact + install.sh,
   154	    #    operator runs on target manually.
   155	    if not t_arch:
   156	        reason = "target arch not specified — cannot match host; producing bundle"
   157	    elif not _local_enabled():
   158	        reason = "OMNISIGHT_T3_LOCAL_ENABLED=false; producing bundle"
   159	    else:
   160	        reason = (
   161	            f"host ({h_arch}/{h_os}) does not match target ({t_arch}/{t_os}); "
   162	            "producing bundle (no SSH/QEMU runner matched)"
   163	        )
   164	    return T3Resolution(
   165	        kind=T3RunnerKind.BUNDLE,
   166	        reason=reason,
   167	        target_arch=t_arch, target_os=t_os,
   168	        host_arch=h_arch, host_os=h_os,
   169	    )

    12	
    13	  * Never bypass Phase 64-A image trust. We literally call

    22	    this at 2: more is pre-warmed waste, 1 is insufficient when
    23	    dispatch fans out.

    25	    get consumed (e.g., DAG mutation) are stopped right away to
    26	    free the lifetime budget for the replanned run.

    30	    no cross-run filesystem residue leaks into the real task.

   136	def pick_prewarm_candidates(dag: DAG, *, depth: int | None = None) -> list[Task]:
   137	    """Return up to `depth` Tier-1 tasks with in-degree 0, in DAG
   138	    declaration order so the selection is deterministic (stable
   139	    replay during incident review)."""
   140	    n = depth if depth is not None else _prewarm_depth()
   141	    if n <= 0:
   142	        return []
   143	    # Count in-degree.
   144	    indeg: dict[str, int] = {t.task_id: 0 for t in dag.tasks}
   145	    for t in dag.tasks:
   146	        for d in t.depends_on:
   147	            if t.task_id in indeg:  # self-referential guard
   148	                indeg[t.task_id] = indeg.get(t.task_id, 0) + (1 if d in indeg else 0)
   149	    ready = [t for t in dag.tasks if indeg.get(t.task_id, 0) == 0]
   150	    # Only Tier-1 benefits from the Docker pre-warm; networked/t3
   151	    # paths have different start-up cost profiles we haven't modelled.
   152	    ready = [t for t in ready if t.required_tier == "t1"]
   153	    return ready[:n]

   164	# untouched: they've already paid their start-up cost, can still be
   165	# consumed, and the H2 backoff in the acquire path provides the
   166	# ultimate gate before they actually run real work.

   170	# auxiliary signal documented on host_metrics.HIGH_PRESSURE_LOADAVG_RATIO.
   171

   173	PREWARM_PAUSE_REASON_MEM = "host_mem_high"

   175	PREWARM_PAUSE_REASON_LOADAVG = "host_loadavg_high"

   178	def _check_host_pressure() -> Optional[str]:
   179	    """Return a reason code if the host is high-pressure, else None.
   180	
   181	    First consults the H2 CPU/mem/container precondition (same source
   182	    of truth as ``_ModeSlot.acquire()`` so prewarm pause and acquire
   183	    deferral never disagree about whether the host is hot). Then falls
   184	    back to the WSL2 loadavg ratio so a host where psutil reports clean
   185	    but the kernel run-queue is saturated still gates new warmups.
   186	
   187	    Failures importing either module return None (allow) — pre-warm is
   188	    an optimisation, never a correctness gate.
   189	    """
   190	    try:
   191	        from backend import decision_engine as _de
   192	        reason = _de._host_precondition_reason()
   193	        if reason:
   194	            return reason
   195	    except Exception as exc:
   196	        logger.debug("prewarm pressure check (decision_engine) failed: %s", exc)
   197	    try:
   198	        from backend import host_metrics as _hm
   199	        if _hm.is_host_high_pressure():
   200	            return PREWARM_PAUSE_REASON_LOADAVG
   201	    except Exception as exc:
   202	        logger.debug("prewarm pressure check (host_metrics) failed: %s", exc)
   203	    return None

    72	def _load_ssh_credentials() -> list[dict]:
    73	    """Load SSH target credentials from ssh_credentials.yaml or
    74	    platform profile deploy fields."""
    75	    import yaml
    76	    from backend.config import settings
    77	
    78	    candidates = []
    79	    if settings.ssh_credentials_file:
    80	        candidates.append(Path(settings.ssh_credentials_file).expanduser())
    81	    candidates.append(_PROJECT_ROOT / "configs" / "ssh_credentials.yaml")
    82	    candidates.append(Path("~/.config/omnisight/ssh_credentials.yaml").expanduser())
    83	
    84	    for path in candidates:
    85	        try:
    86	            resolved = path.resolve(strict=False)
    87	            if resolved.exists():
    88	                data = yaml.safe_load(resolved.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    89	                targets = data.get("targets", [])
    90	                if isinstance(targets, list):
    91	                    logger.info("Loaded %d SSH targets from %s", len(targets), resolved)
    92	                    return targets
    93	        except Exception as exc:
    94	            logger.warning("SSH credential load from %s failed: %s", path, exc)
    95	
    96	    return []

    99	_SSH_CRED_CACHE: list[dict] | None = None
   100	_SSH_CRED_LOCK = threading.Lock()

   103	def get_ssh_targets() -> list[dict]:
   104	    global _SSH_CRED_CACHE
   105	    cached = _SSH_CRED_CACHE
   106	    if cached is not None:
   107	        return list(cached)
   108	    with _SSH_CRED_LOCK:
   109	        if _SSH_CRED_CACHE is not None:
   110	            return list(_SSH_CRED_CACHE)
   111	        _SSH_CRED_CACHE = _load_ssh_credentials()
   112	        return list(_SSH_CRED_CACHE)
   113

   115	def clear_ssh_credential_cache() -> None:
   116	    global _SSH_CRED_CACHE
   117	    with _SSH_CRED_LOCK:
   118	        _SSH_CRED_CACHE = None

   121	def find_target_for_arch(target_arch: str, target_os: str = "linux") -> SSHTarget | None:
   122	    """Find a registered SSH target matching the requested arch/os."""
   123	    from backend.routers.system import _canon_arch
   124	
   125	    wanted = _canon_arch(target_arch)
   126	    for entry in get_ssh_targets():
   127	        entry_arch = _canon_arch(entry.get("arch", ""))
   128	        entry_os = (entry.get("os", "linux")).lower()
   129	        if entry_arch == wanted and entry_os == target_os.lower():
   130	            return SSHTarget(
   131	                host=entry.get("host", ""),
   132	                port=int(entry.get("port", 22)),
   133	                user=entry.get("user", "root"),
   134	                key_path=entry.get("key_path", "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"),
   135	                sysroot_path=entry.get("sysroot_path", ""),
   136	                scratch_dir=entry.get("scratch_dir", "/tmp/omnisight"),
   137	            )
   138	
   139	    # Fallback: check platform profile deploy fields
   140	    try:
   141	        import yaml
   142	        from backend.platform_profile import _NON_PROFILE_FILES  # W0 #274 (renamed in FX.9.3)
   143	        platforms_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / "configs" / "platforms"
   144	        for yf in platforms_dir.glob("*.yaml"):
   145	            if yf.name in _NON_PROFILE_FILES:
   146	                continue
   147	            data = yaml.safe_load(yf.read_text()) or {}
   148	            profile_arch = _canon_arch(data.get("kernel_arch") or data.get("arch") or "")
   149	            if profile_arch == wanted and data.get("deploy_method") == "ssh":
   150	                host = data.get("deploy_target_ip", "")
   151	                if host:
   152	                    return SSHTarget(
   153	                        host=host,
   154	                        port=int(data.get("deploy_port", 22)),
   155	                        user=data.get("deploy_user", "root"),
   156	                        key_path=data.get("ssh_key", "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"),
   157	                        sysroot_path=data.get("sysroot_path", ""),
   158	                        scratch_dir=data.get("deploy_path", "/tmp/omnisight"),
   159	                    )
   160	    except Exception as exc:
   161	        logger.debug("Platform profile SSH fallback failed: %s", exc)
   162	
   163	    return None
