   165	
   166	def _connect(target: SSHTarget) -> "paramiko.SSHClient":
   167	    """Create and return a connected SSH client."""
   168	    _require_paramiko()
   169	    client = paramiko.SSHClient()
   170	    client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())
   171	
   172	    known_hosts = Path("~/.ssh/known_hosts").expanduser()
   173	    if known_hosts.exists():
   174	        client.load_host_keys(str(known_hosts))
   175	
   176	    key_path = _resolve_key_path(target.key_path)
   177	    if not Path(key_path).exists():
   178	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"SSH key not found: {key_path}")
   179	
   180	    key_stat = os.stat(key_path)
   181	    if key_stat.st_mode & (stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IROTH):
   182	        raise PermissionError(
   183	            f"SSH key {key_path} has group/other read permissions — "
   184	            "SSH will refuse it. Run: chmod 600 " + key_path
   185	        )
   186	
   187	    client.connect(
   188	        hostname=target.host,
   189	        port=target.port,
   190	        username=target.user,
   191	        key_filename=key_path,
   192	        timeout=15,
   193	        allow_agent=False,
   194	        look_for_keys=False,
   195	    )
   196	    return client
   197	
   198	
   199	def _setup_sandbox(
   200	    client: paramiko.SSHClient,
   201	    target: SSHTarget,
   202	) -> str:
   203	    """Create per-run scratch directory on the remote. Returns the path.
   204	    If sysroot is specified, verify it exists and is read-only."""
   205	    scratch = target.scratch_dir.rstrip("/") + f"/run-{int(time.time())}"
   206	    _exec_sync(client, f"mkdir -p {scratch}")
   207	
   208	    if target.sysroot_path:
   209	        rc, out = _exec_sync(client, f"test -d {target.sysroot_path} && echo OK")
   210	        if "OK" not in out:
   211	            logger.warning("Sysroot %s not found on remote", target.sysroot_path)
   212	        else:
   213	            rc, mount_out = _exec_sync(
   214	                client,
   215	                f"mount | grep '{target.sysroot_path}' | grep -q 'ro,' && echo RO"
   216	            )
   217	            if "RO" not in mount_out:
   218	                logger.warning(
   219	                    "Sysroot %s is not mounted read-only — safety degraded",
   220	                    target.sysroot_path,
   221	                )
   222	
   223	    return scratch
   224	
   225	
   226	def _exec_sync(
   227	    client: paramiko.SSHClient,
   228	    command: str,
   229	    timeout: int = 30,
   230	) -> tuple[int, str]:
   231	    """Execute a command synchronously, return (exit_code, output)."""
   232	    _, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command(command, timeout=timeout)
   233	    out = stdout.read().decode(errors="replace")
   234	    err = stderr.read().decode(errors="replace")
   235	    rc = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
   236	    combined = out
   237	    if err:
   238	        combined += f"\n[STDERR] {err}" if out else err
   239	    return rc, combined.strip()
   240

   188	    """Append one JSON object as a line. Creates parent dirs. Never truncates
   189	    — the consumer keeps the newest matching record, so history is fine."""

   199	def _gerrit_query_argv(
   200	    *, host: str, port: int, key_path: Path | None, query: str
   201	) -> list[str]:
   202	    argv = ["ssh"]
   203	    if key_path is not None:
   204	        argv += ["-i", str(key_path)]
   205	    argv += [
   206	        "-p", str(port),
   207	        "-o", "BatchMode=yes",
   208	        "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new",
   209	        host,
   210	        "gerrit", "query",
   211	        "--format=JSON",
   212	        # Required on Gerrit 3.13: ``gerrit query`` no longer emits the
   213	        # ``currentPatchSet`` block by default (see OP-959 and
   214	        # ``release_milestone_checker.SshGerritClient._query``).
   215	        "--current-patch-set",
   216	        query,
   217	    ]
   218	    return argv
   219	
   220	
   221	def resolve_develop_tip(
   222	    *,
   223	    runner: Runner,
   224	    host: str,
   225	    port: int,
   226	    key_path: Path | None,
   227	    project: str,
   228	    timeout: int = 30,
   229	) -> str:
   230	    """Return the develop-tip commit SHA Gerrit currently has merged.
   231	
   232	    Mirrors ``release_milestone_checker.SshGerritClient.develop_tip`` so the
   233	    ``revision`` we stamp into the JSONL line matches the one the checker
   234	    queries for that gate. Raises ``RuntimeError`` on any failure — the
   235	    caller turns that into exit code 3 (we cannot honestly emit a gate
   236	    status without knowing which revision it is for).
   237	    """
   238	    argv = _gerrit_query_argv(
   239	        host=host, port=port, key_path=key_path,
   240	        query=f"project:{project} branch:{BRANCH} status:merged",
   241	    )
   242	    proc = runner(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, check=True)
   243	    for raw in (proc.stdout or "").splitlines():
   244	        try:
   245	            row = json.loads(raw)
   246	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   247	            continue
   248	        if not isinstance(row, dict) or row.get("type") == "stats":
   249	            continue
   250	        revision = str((row.get("currentPatchSet") or {}).get("revision") or "")
   251	        if revision:
   252	            return revision
   253	    raise RuntimeError(
   254	        "Gerrit develop query returned no merged change with "
   255	        "currentPatchSet.revision (expected `gerrit query --current-patch-set`)"
   256	    )

   152	def _headers() -> dict[str, str]:
   153	    # User-Agent is mandatory against CF-fronted prod — the default
   154	    # `Python-urllib/3.x` signature is flagged by Cloudflare Bot Fight
   155	    # Mode (Error 1010 "browser_signature_banned"). Ship an explicit
   156	    # named-tool UA so the smoke test is attributable in edge logs
   157	    # and passes reputation gates. Override via OMNISIGHT_SMOKE_UA if
   158	    # the operator ever needs to impersonate a specific client.
   159	    ua = os.environ.get(
   160	        "OMNISIGHT_SMOKE_UA",
   161	        "OmniSight-SmokeTest/1.0 (+https://github.com/limit5/OmniSight-Productizer)",
   162	    )
   163	    h = {
   164	        "Content-Type": "application/json",
   165	        "Accept": "application/json",
   166	        "User-Agent": ua,
   167	    }
   168	    if TOKEN:
   169	        h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {TOKEN}"
   170	    # Optional session cookie for callers that already have one; no
   171	    # longer required since auth_baseline now recognises Bearer tokens
   172	    # directly (fixed 2026-04-24, see backend/auth_baseline.py
   173	    # _has_valid_bearer_token). Retained so an operator who wants to
   174	    # hit the smoke script from a logged-in browser context can still
   175	    # pass OMNISIGHT_SESSION_COOKIE without also provisioning an API
   176	    # token.
   177	    session = os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_SESSION_COOKIE", "").strip()
   178	    if session:
   179	        h["Cookie"] = f"omnisight_session={session}"
   180	    return h

   183	def _post(path: str, body: dict) -> dict:
   184	    url = f"{API}{path}"
   185	    data = json.dumps(body).encode()
   186	    req = request.Request(url, data=data, headers=_headers(), method="POST")
   187	    try:
   188	        with request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
   189	            return json.loads(resp.read())
   190	    except urlerror.HTTPError as exc:
   191	        resp_body = exc.read().decode(errors="replace")
   192	        print(f"  HTTP {exc.code}: {resp_body}", file=sys.stderr)
   193	        raise
   194

   221	def poll_run(run_id: str) -> dict:
   222	    """Poll workflow run until terminal status or timeout."""
   223	    deadline = time.time() + POLL_TIMEOUT
   224	    while time.time() < deadline:
   225	        run = _get(f"/workflow/runs/{run_id}")
   226	        status = run.get("run", {}).get("status", run.get("status", "unknown"))
   227	        if status in ("completed", "failed", "halted"):
   228	            return run
   229	        print(f"  ... status={status}, waiting {POLL_INTERVAL}s")
   230	        time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL)
   231	    print(f"  TIMEOUT after {POLL_TIMEOUT}s", file=sys.stderr)
   232	    return {}

     1	"""[OP-1643] Boreas-B A2 — dev/prod env-contract guard.
     2	
     3	Fail-closed when a process's declared environment (``OMNISIGHT_ENV``) does not
     4	match the environment its resolved Postgres DSN points at. This is the
     5	*env-declaration* layer that complements A1's *DB-credential* layer (the
     6	``omnisight_dev`` role is ``REVOKE``'d ``CONNECT`` on the prod ``omnisight`` DB):
     7	A1 catches a dev process by its credential; A2 catches a dev process that
     8	resolves a prod-looking DSN regardless of credential.
     9	
    10	Design + codex review: ``docs/sprint-boreas/boreas-b-A2-env-contract-guard-design.md``.
    11	
    12	This module is intentionally dependency-light (stdlib only) and must NOT import
    13	``backend.config`` / ``backend.db_url`` — it is called *from* the connection
    14	primitives (``db_pool.init_pool``, ``db._resolve_pg_dsn``,
    15	``db_url.DatabaseURL.asyncpg_connect_kwargs``, ``alembic/env.py``), so importing
    16	those back would create a cycle. It ships its own tolerant DSN parser.

    27	# matching backend.config.ConfigValidationError.

    29

    31	_DEV_PORTS = {58432}

    34	# Canonical env aliases (mirrors backend.config._resolve_yaml_path + the
    35	# startup validator, which only special-cased the literal "production").
    36	_ENV_ALIASES = {
    37	    "production": "prod",
    38	    "prod": "prod",
    39	    "develop": "dev",
    40	    "development": "dev",

    46	class EnvContractViolation(SystemExit):
    47	    """Raised (exits 78) when env declaration and DB DSN disagree."""
    48	
    49	    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
    50	        super().__init__(_EXIT_CONFIG)
    51	        self.message = message
    52	        _logger.critical("EnvContractViolation: %s", message)

    55	def canonical_env(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
    56	    """Canonicalize ``OMNISIGHT_ENV`` → ``dev`` / ``staging`` / ``prod`` / None.
    57	
    58	    Unknown non-empty values are returned lower-cased as-is (so an unexpected
    59	    marker is treated as its own class and will fail the match, fail-closed).
    60	    """
    61	    if raw is None:
    62	        return None
    63	    v = raw.strip().lower()
    64	    if not v:
    65	        return None
    66	    return _ENV_ALIASES.get(v, v)
    67	
    68	
    69	def _split_dsn(dsn: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, int | None]:
    70	    """Tolerant parse → (user, db-name, port).
    71	
    72	    Avoids ``urllib.parse`` pitfalls with passwords containing ``/`` or ``@``:
    73	    the userinfo is everything up to the LAST ``@`` (libpq convention), and the
    74	    db-name is taken only from the path AFTER userinfo is stripped, so a ``/``
    75	    inside the password cannot be mistaken for the path separator.
    76	    """
    77	    from urllib.parse import unquote
    78	
    79	    rest = dsn.split("://", 1)[1] if "://" in dsn else dsn
    80	    at = rest.rfind("@")
    81	    userinfo = rest[:at] if at >= 0 else ""
    82	    authority = rest[at + 1:] if at >= 0 else rest
    83	
    84	    user = None
    85	    if userinfo:
    86	        user = unquote(userinfo.split(":", 1)[0]) or None
    87	
    88	    hostport, _, pathq = authority.partition("/")
    89	    db = pathq.split("?", 1)[0].strip("/")
    90	    db = unquote(db) if db else None
    91	
    92	    port: int | None = None
    93	    if ":" in hostport:
    94	        tail = hostport.rsplit(":", 1)[1]
    95	        if tail.isdigit():
    96	            port = int(tail)
    97	    return user, db, port
    98	
    99	
   100	def classify_dsn(dsn: str | None) -> str:
   101	    """Classify a DSN → ``"prod"`` / ``"dev"`` / ``"staging"`` / ``"sqlite"`` /
   102	    ``"skip"`` / ``"unknown"``.
   103	
   104	    - ``skip``    — empty, or a non-Postgres non-SQLite scheme (not our concern).
   105	    - ``sqlite``  — a SQLite URL (legacy / tests).
   106	    - ``unknown`` — a Postgres URL we cannot positively place (fail-closed: the
   107	      caller hard-fails on this, so a typo / renamed-prod / url-encoding bug
   108	      can't fail-open).
   109	    """
   110	    if not dsn or not dsn.strip():
   111	        return "skip"
   112	    s = dsn.strip()
   113	    scheme = s.split("://", 1)[0].lower() if "://" in s else s.lower()
   114	    if scheme.startswith("sqlite"):
   115	        return "sqlite"
   116	    if not scheme.startswith(("postgresql", "postgres", "asyncpg")):
   117	        return "skip"  # mysql/etc — not the omnisight PG we guard
   118	
   119	    user, db, port = _split_dsn(s)
   120	    db_l = (db or "").lower()
   121	    user_l = (user or "").lower()
   122	
   123	    if db_l.endswith(("_dev", "-dev")) or user_l == "omnisight_dev" or (port in _DEV_PORTS):
   124	        return "dev"
   125	    if db_l.endswith(("_staging", "-staging")) or (port in _STAGING_PORTS):
   126	        return "staging"
   127	    if db_l == "omnisight" and user_l == "omnisight":
   128	        return "prod"
   129	    return "unknown"
   130	
   131	
   132	def _truthy(val: str | None) -> bool:
   133	    return (val or "").strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
   134	
   135	
   136	def enforce_env_db_contract(
   137	    dsn: str | None,
   138	    *,
   139	    source: str,
   140	    env: str | None = None,
   141	) -> None:
   142	    """Fail closed (exit 78) when ``OMNISIGHT_ENV`` disagrees with ``dsn``.
   143	
   144	    ``source`` is a short label for the call site (for the error/log message).
   145	    ``env`` overrides ``OMNISIGHT_ENV`` (used by tests). See the design doc for
   146	    the full truth table; summary:
   147	
   148	    ===============  ==========  =======
   149	    OMNISIGHT_ENV    DSN class   verdict
   150	    ===============  ==========  =======
   151	    dev              dev          OK
   152	    dev              prod/stg     FAIL  (core protection)
   153	    prod             prod         OK
   154	    prod             dev/stg      FAIL  (symmetric)
   155	    unset            prod         OK    (legacy prod-by-default: runners/coord)
   156	    unset            dev/stg      FAIL  (non-prod DB without declaring non-prod)
   157	    any              unknown-pg   FAIL  (fail-closed on unrecognised PG)
   158	    any              sqlite/skip  OK    (legacy/tests/non-PG)
   159	    ===============  ==========  =======
   160	    """
   161	    cls = classify_dsn(dsn)
   162	    if cls in ("sqlite", "skip"):
   163	        return
   164	
   165	    canon_env = canonical_env(env if env is not None else os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_ENV"))
   166	    redacted = _redact(dsn or "")
   167	
   168	    # Break-glass: refused in prod (env OR DSN) so it can never silence a real
   169	    # prod mismatch; valid prod states (unset+prod / prod+prod) never need it.
   170	    if _truthy(os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_ENV_CONTRACT_DISABLE")):
   171	        if canon_env == "prod" or cls == "prod":
   172	            raise EnvContractViolation(
   173	                f"OMNISIGHT_ENV_CONTRACT_DISABLE=1 is refused when env or DSN is prod "
   174	                f"(env={canon_env!r}, dsn-class={cls!r}, source={source}, dsn={redacted})."
   175	            )
   176	        _logger.warning(
   177	            "env-contract DISABLED via OMNISIGHT_ENV_CONTRACT_DISABLE=1 "
   178	            "(env=%r, dsn-class=%r, source=%s) — break-glass, non-prod only.",
   179	            canon_env, cls, source,
   180	        )
   181	        return
   182	
   183	    # Test/CI carveout: tests call init_pool/connect directly with assorted
   184	    # DSNs. Bypass ONLY when not pointed at prod — a prod DSN inside a test is
   185	    # still a real violation worth surfacing.
   186	    in_test = bool(os.environ.get("PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST")) or _truthy(os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_CI_MODE"))
   187	    if in_test and cls != "prod":
   188	        return
   189	
   190	    # Unrecognised Postgres → hard fail (never fail-open).
   191	    if cls == "unknown":
   192	        raise EnvContractViolation(
   193	            f"DSN resolves to an unrecognised Postgres database — refusing to connect "
   194	            f"(env={canon_env!r}, source={source}, dsn={redacted}). Expected a db/user "
   195	            f"matching dev (omnisight_dev), staging (*_staging) or prod (omnisight)."
   196	        )
   197	
   198	    # cls is one of dev/staging/prod from here.
   199	    expected = "prod" if canon_env is None else canon_env
   200	    if cls != expected:
   201	        env_desc = "unset (legacy prod-by-default)" if canon_env is None else repr(canon_env)
   202	        raise EnvContractViolation(
   203	            f"env-contract violation: OMNISIGHT_ENV={env_desc} but the DSN looks like "
   204	            f"'{cls}' (source={source}, dsn={redacted}). A '{expected}' process must use a "
   205	            f"'{expected}' database. Set OMNISIGHT_ENV to match, or point at the correct DB."
   206	        )
   207	
   208	
   209	def _redact(dsn: str) -> str:
   210	    """Mask the password in a DSN for safe logging."""
   211	    if "://" not in dsn or "@" not in dsn:
   212	        return dsn
   213	    scheme, rest = dsn.split("://", 1)
   214	    at = rest.rfind("@")
   215	    userinfo, tail = rest[:at], rest[at + 1:]
   216	    if ":" in userinfo:
   217	        userinfo = userinfo.split(":", 1)[0] + ":***"
   218	    return f"{scheme}://{userinfo}@{tail}"

docs/adr/ADR-0033-governance-engine-and-operator-authority.md:110:                                  # values: 'key-material' | 'meta-closure' | 'release-tag-governance' | 'override' | 'roster-mutation' | <custom>
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:3:title: Single-trunk Release Train — retire `main`, tag-driven releases
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:8:# ADR-0040 — Single-trunk Release Train (retire `main`, tag-driven releases)
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:12:**Supersedes**: ADR-0001 (Five-branch Git Flow), ADR-0020 (Release cut to `main` as a single merge change), ADR-0039 (Release-cut submit-requirement hashtag/applicableIf), ADR-0016 (D5 develop→main promotion — already historical). Obsoletes the `develop→main` promotion portions of ADR-0010 (Deployment Automation Gates) and ADR-0011 (Sprint D plan).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:14:**Amends**: ADR-0017 (Release conductor), ADR-0018 (Event-driven release pipeline), ADR-0019 (`release:force-promote` override), ADR-0021 (Release Pipeline Coordinator).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:24:ADR-0001 adopted full GitFlow (5 long-lived branch types) on 2026-05-04 to handle multi-AI parallelism. In practice (2026-05): `develop` and `main` diverged continuously; `main` rotted **175 commits** behind develop; the operator repeatedly force-aligned `main` and hard-cut releases. The develop→main release-cut machinery (ADR-0016 → ADR-0020) wedged on 2nd+ cuts (AUDIT-26), and its `auto_promote_main` consumer was never activated (AUDIT-26d). Meanwhile the GitLab CI image pipeline (ADR-0038) is **tag-driven and branch-agnostic** (`workflow: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /^v.*/`) and already builds prod images successfully (pipeline #32 = v0.5.0-rc5-hotfix4). Prod has de-facto been running tagged **develop** commits; `main` had no real consumer.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:26:GitFlow's two-long-lived-branch model is designed for versioned, multi-release software, not a continuously-delivered web app with fast AI-driven velocity. The drift, churn, and wedging are inherent to that mismatch.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:30:Adopt a **single-trunk Release Train**:
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:33:2. **`main` is retired.** No develop→main merge, no FF-from-release, no promotion to main.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:34:3. **A release = a promoted IMAGE tag + digest recorded in `release_train`** (NOT a `v*` git tag — see Decision RT-20 below; a git tag would trigger the existing CI `^v` build rule and rebuild a different digest, breaking "validated digest == shipped digest"). Candidate images are built from a chosen develop SHA via pipeline-API (`CANDIDATE_SHA`); promotion retags the validated digest to `vX.Y.Z` in GitLab CR.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:35:4. **No `release/X.Y` branches.** Hotfixes are also tags (`v0.6.1`) cut from develop. **Every `v*` tag MUST be a prod-usable build** — there is no stabilisation branch to repair on.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:50:**Migration blast radius** (must change atomically with retiring main — see `memory: project_retire_main_blast_radius_audit` + codex audit `/tmp/retire-main-release-train-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt`): 5 live `main`-hardcoded landmines (`scripts/deploy-prod.sh`, `backend/agents/auto_tag_release.py`, `scripts/staging_deploy.sh`, `backend/routers/webhooks.py`, `.gerrit/project.config` Human-Plus-2 carve-out). Plus deletion of dormant promote machinery, retirement of the release-branch family, ~6 ADR cross-ref updates, and dedup of the duplicate `NNNN-*.md` / `ADR-NNNN-*.md` ADR files.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:54:These MUST be resolved before this ADR moves Proposed → Accepted. Full audit: `/tmp/retire-main-release-train-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt`.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:56:1. **Candidate-artifact circular dependency (the deepest hole).** `scripts/sync_staging_to_develop.sh` stages an image tagged with the raw develop SHA, but the GitLab pipeline only builds on `v*` tags (publishes `${tag}`, `sha-${short}`, `latest`) — it never builds a raw develop-SHA image. So "validate on staging BEFORE cutting the tag" is impossible: the candidate image doesn't exist until a tag exists. **Must pick a candidate-artifact model first**: (a) build immutable images for every accepted develop commit (branch pipeline → `sha-${short}`), or (b) auto-create an `rc`/pre-release tag, stage THAT, then promote to final `v*`, or (c) accept that the final tag exists pre-validation and gate DEPLOY (not the tag). Each has different operator semantics.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:57:2. **"Every tag prod-usable" has no test gate.** `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no test/lint stage; Gerrit `Verified` is disabled (`applicableIf=is:false`). A `v*` tag can build+sign+attest without ever proving the suite passed at that SHA — and a bad tag is a *permanent* release object. Auto-cut needs a real per-SHA green signal (pytest + FE build/typecheck + migration check + smoke/canary) before it may tag.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:58:3. **Hotfix isolation gap (stop-the-line policy needed).** With no stabilisation branch, `v0.6.1` from develop ships *every* later develop commit too. Need an explicit written policy: revert/disable unready develop changes before tagging, OR a defined tag-from-last-release-tag exception.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:61:6. **FE feature-flag is net-new work, not a flip.** Existing `backend/routers/feature_flags.py` is an operator/admin registry (leaks owner/rollout/tenant). Need: a frontend-safe `GET /api/feature-flags/effective` (public booleans only, server-evaluated, fail-closed), an FE provider/hook + SSR bootstrap, and **fix the tier-enum drift** (backend `debug/dogfood/early_access/staged/ga` vs FE `debug/dogfood/preview/release/runtime`).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:66:1. **Freeze old release automation** (disable auto-promote-main, auto-promote-develop, auto-tag-release, release-cut guards) before any behaviour change.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:70:5. **Add FE runtime flags** before the first trunk release carrying incomplete UI.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:71:6. **Replace Gerrit main/release rules with develop/tag gates**; decide whether `Verified` becomes active on develop.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:72:7. **Update conductor/coordinator** to key release identity on immutable tag/SHA/digest, not main promotion.

docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:89:- **Candidate-artifact model = revised Model A** (`docs/design/2026-05-21-model-a-candidate-build-release-train.md`): build `sha-<fullsha>` from a chosen green develop SHA via pipeline-API; validate on staging by digest; promote = retag the SAME digest to the reserved `vX.Y.Z`. docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:90:- **RT-20 (final release identity) = IMAGE-TAG-ONLY.** No `v*` git tag is created (avoids the CI-rebuild hazard with zero fragility — no need to special-case the CI workflow rule). Release identity = promoted GitLab CR image tag `vX.Y.Z` (→ validated digest) + `release_train`/`release_audit` row. Git/human provenance = the audit row (git_sha + digests); optionally a NON-`v*`-matching ref like `released/vX.Y.Z` created post-promote (CI never fires on it). Rationale: prod already runs pinned images not git refs; main is retired; the audit row is the authoritative record; avoids fragile CI tag-exclusion logic.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:91:- **RT-21 (bridge) = release-train tracks BACKEND + FRONTEND digests only (a PAIR, not a triplet).** Verified this session: prod compose deploys backend-a/b + frontend (no bridge container); the gerrit-jira-bridge/coordinator run as host daemons from the `sora-bridge` develop checkout (control-plane, separate concern). The `bridge` image build is decoupled from the release-train promote/deploy gate. (If bridge is ever containerised into prod, add it then.)

   488	async def _record_step(run_id: str, idempotency_key: str,
   489	                       output: Any, error: str | None) -> StepRecord:
   490	    """Atomically insert a finished step. UNIQUE constraint catches a
   491	    race with another writer — in which case we read back the existing
   492	    record and return that (last writer wins on raw run, but for
   493	    idempotency the cached output is what we want anyway).
   494	
   495	    SP-5.6a: INSERT + UPDATE now run inside a single tx so the
   496	    last_step_id bump on workflow_runs is committed with the
   497	    workflow_steps row (previously under compat a crash between
   498	    statements could leave the step recorded but last_step_id
   499	    pointing at a prior step — visible to replay() as an
   500	    inconsistency). On UNIQUE-violation we roll back explicitly via
   501	    the ``async with transaction()`` exception path and fall through
   502	    to the idempotency re-read.
   503	    """
   504	    step = StepRecord(
   505	        id=_uid("step"), run_id=run_id, idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
   506	        started_at=time.time(), completed_at=time.time(),
   507	        output=output, error=error,
   508	    )
   509	    try:
   510	        async with get_pool().acquire() as conn:
   511	            async with conn.transaction():
   512	                await conn.execute(
   513	                    "INSERT INTO workflow_steps "
   514	                    "(id, run_id, idempotency_key, started_at, "
   515	                    " completed_at, output_json, error) "
   516	                    "VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)",
   517	                    step.id, step.run_id, step.idempotency_key,
   518	                    step.started_at, step.completed_at,
   519	                    json.dumps(output) if output is not None else None,
   520	                    error,
   590	    }

     2	
     3	Single source of truth for "is this project a same-arch host-native
     4	build?" + "should we shortcut the pipeline to the 4-phase app_only
     5	flow?". Used by:
     6	
     7	  - decision_engine.propose() injects is_host_native into source so
     8	    chooser confidence can step up
     9	  - forecast.py reads project_track to pick task templates
    10	  - pipeline.py (Phase 59 v2 — out of scope for this commit) will
    11	    branch on app_only_pipeline()
    12	
    13	Reads `hardware_manifest.yaml` lazily; results cached for 60s so the
    14	hot path doesn't hit disk on every decision propose.
    15	"""
    16	
    17	from __future__ import annotations
    18	
    19	import logging
    20	import os
    21	import platform
    22	import time
    23	from pathlib import Path
    24	
    25	import yaml
    26	
    27	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    28	
    29	_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    30	_CACHE_TTL_S = 60.0
    31	_cache: tuple[float, dict] | None = None
    32	
    33	
    34	def _read_manifest() -> dict:
    35	    """Read + cache hardware_manifest.yaml. Returns {} on any error."""
    36	    global _cache
    37	    now = time.time()
    38	    if _cache and (now - _cache[0]) < _CACHE_TTL_S:
    39	        return _cache[1]
    40	    path = _PROJECT_ROOT / "configs" / "hardware_manifest.yaml"
    41	    if not path.exists():
    42	        _cache = (now, {})
    43	        return {}
    44	    try:
    45	        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    46	    except Exception as exc:
    47	        logger.debug("manifest read failed: %s", exc)
    48	        data = {}
    49	    _cache = (now, data)
    50	    return data
    51	
    52	
    53	def _bust_cache() -> None:
    54	    global _cache
    55	    _cache = None
    56	
    57	
    58	_HOST_ARCH_ALIASES = {
    59	    "x86_64": "x86_64", "amd64": "x86_64",
    60	    "aarch64": "arm64", "arm64": "arm64",
    61	    "armv7l": "arm32", "armv7": "arm32",
    62	    "riscv64": "riscv64",
    63	}
    64	
    65	
    66	def host_arch_canonical() -> str:
    67	    raw = platform.machine().lower().strip()
    68	    return _HOST_ARCH_ALIASES.get(raw, raw)
    69

   280	serving flash/UART/i2c operations against a physically attached
   281	target. That still applies for **cross-architecture** deployments
   282	(x86_64 host → arm64 board). But for **same-architecture**
   283	deployments (AMD x86_64 host → x86_64 industrial PC, or just
   284	localhost) the daemon is overkill.
   285	
   286	T3-LOCAL short-circuits: when `t3_resolver` detects
   287	`host_arch == target_arch && host_os == target_os`, t3 tasks run in
   288	a t1-style runsc sandbox on the host, with `--network host` so
   289	smoke-tests can hit localhost services. Validator `tier_violation`
   290	relaxes for the matching target — a t3 step with `toolchain: cmake`
   291	validates fine when the resolver picks LOCAL.
   292	
   293	| Control | Env | Default |
   294	|---|---|---|
   295	| Runner kill-switch | `OMNISIGHT_T3_LOCAL_ENABLED` | `true` |
   296	| Target profile override (per submit) | `target_platform` field in `POST /dag` body | (inherits `configs/hardware_manifest.yaml::target_platform`) |
   297	
   298	### Resolution pipeline
   299	
   300	```
   301	required_tier=t3 task → resolve_t3_runner(target_arch, target_os)
   302	  ├─ host_arch == target_arch  AND  host_os == target_os
   303	  │   AND  OMNISIGHT_T3_LOCAL_ENABLED=true   → LOCAL  ⚡
   304	  └─ otherwise                                → BUNDLE 🔗
   305	     (scp artefact + install.sh to the real target)
   306	```
   307	
   308	The Ops Summary panel shows a LOCAL / BUNDLE breakdown; the DAG
   309	Canvas shows a ⚡ (LOCAL) or 🔗 (bundle) chip on every t3 node so
   310	the operator can see at a glance whether a plan will run fully on
   311	the host or needs an artefact handoff.
   312	
   313	### Force BUNDLE for paranoid deployments
   314	
   315	Set `OMNISIGHT_T3_LOCAL_ENABLED=false`. Every t3 task then routes
   316	through the BUNDLE path even when host matches target — useful for
   317	security audits where "the host is also the target" is considered
   318	too much overlap.
   319	
   320	### Still refuses dangerous toolchains under LOCAL
   321	
   322	The tier-swap (t3 → check against t1 rules when LOCAL) is a full
   323	substitution, not an allow-list merge. A `flash_board` toolchain is
   324	not in t1's allowed list, so it's rejected even on the LOCAL path.
   325	You can't pretend to flash a board over localhost.
   326	
   327	### Related files
   328	
   329	- `backend/t3_resolver.py` — resolver + `T3RunnerKind` + metric
   330	- `backend/container.py::start_t3_local_container` — T3-LOCAL runner
   331	- `backend/container.py::dispatch_t3` — resolver entry point
   332	- `backend/dag_validator.py::_check_tier_capability` — tier swap
   333	- `configs/platforms/host_native.yaml` — "use the host" profile

     1	"""OP-1106 v2-Ⅹ-1bc — runner_claims table for runner coordination substrate.
     2	
     3	Revision ID: 0236
     4	Revises: 0235
     5	Create Date: 2026-05-15
     6	backwards-compat: safe
     7	
     8	Per spec docs/sprint-s12/sprint-s12g-A-v2-runtime-defense-contract-spec.md
     9	§3 Family ⑩ §4. Foundation table for the runner coordination substrate
    10	that replaces JIRA-label-based mutex (OP-977) over the next Atlas tickets:
    11	
    12	* OP-1107 (X-2-Shadow) wires the shadow dual-write integration
    13	* OP-1108 (X-2bc) replaces ``find_mutex_holders()`` JQL read path with
    14	  ``find_active_holders()`` (this table)
    15	* OP-1109 (X-2d) cuts claim acquisition over in the 3 runner entry points
    16	* OP-1110 (X-2-Cutover) drops the label-based writes
    17	
    18	This migration is **shadow-only at land time**: writes happen but no
    19	read consumer exists. That keeps it deploy-safe — rolling forward and
    20	back never breaks an active runner because nothing reads the table yet.
    21	
    22	Schema rationale
    23	----------------
    24	* ``lease_id`` is a client-generated UUID4. It's the primary key so the
    25	  caller can hold + reference a lease without round-trip surrogate-key
    26	  reads, and so the application's release/heartbeat paths don't need
    27	  to look up the row by composite key.
    28	* ``resource_key`` is the mutex resource (typically
    29	  ``mutex:<file-path>`` or ``mutex:<jira-key>``). A **partial unique
    30	  index** on ``(resource_key) WHERE state = 'active'`` enforces
    31	  at-most-one active claim per resource. SQLite 3.8+ and Postgres both
    32	  support partial unique indexes — INSERT conflicts surface as
    33	  IntegrityError → wrapped to ``ClaimBlocked`` in the module layer.
    34	* ``state`` is ``'active'`` or ``'released'`` (closed set, enforced by
    35	  CHECK). Released rows stay in the table as an audit trail; the
    36	  partial index ignores them.
    37	* ``fencing_token`` extends the OP-977 format
    38	  (``claim:{instance}:{epoch_us}-{uuid}``) so callers can reuse
    39	  existing parsing.
    40	* ``external_refs`` is JSON for forward-compat (e.g., Gerrit Change ID,
    41	  worktree path). Stored as JSONB on Postgres, TEXT on SQLite — the
    42	  module layer round-trips it via ``json.dumps`` / ``json.loads``.
    43	"""
    44	from __future__ import annotations

     1	"""OP-1106 / v2-Ⅹ-1bc — Runner coordination substrate (shadow-only at land time).
     2	
     3	Backwards-compat: safe (additive module + table; no consumer reads it yet).
     4	
     5	Provides a 4-function API for runner claim coordination backed by the
     6	``runner_claims`` Postgres/SQLite table (alembic 0234). Replaces the
     7	JIRA-label-based mutex (OP-977's ``find_mutex_holders`` +
     8	``claim_ticket_atomic`` in :mod:`backend.agents.jira_dispatch`) over
     9	the next Atlas tickets:
    10	
    11	* :func:`acquire_claim` — atomic INSERT; raises :class:`ClaimBlocked`
    12	  on resource collision. Idempotent for same-owner re-acquire.
    13	* :func:`release_claim` — soft delete (``state='released'``); fencing
    14	  token must match the active row. Idempotent: releasing an
    15	  already-released or never-existed lease is a no-op.
    16	* :func:`record_phase` — heartbeat + phase tracker on active claim.
    17	  Used by long-running tickets to signal liveness.
    18	* :func:`find_active_holders` — read-side query that replaces the JQL
    19	  ``find_mutex_holders`` once OP-1108 cuts the read path over.
    20	
    21	Fencing token format extends OP-977's
    22	``claim:{instance}:{epoch_us}-{uuid}`` so callers can reuse the
    23	existing label-parsing helpers during the strangler-pattern migration.
    24	
    25	Schema reference: see docstring of
    26	``backend/alembic/versions/0234_runner_claims.py`` §"Schema rationale".
    27	
    28	Why sqlite3 (sync) and not asyncpg/aiosqlite
    29	--------------------------------------------
    30	The three runner entry points
    31	(``auto-runner-jira.py`` / ``auto-runner-multi.py`` /
    32	``auto-runner-codex.py``) are sync code paths. Wrapping them in async
    33	just for the claim layer would force every caller to bridge contexts;
    34	the claim path is also short-lived (single INSERT/UPDATE per
    35	transition) so the sync ergonomics win. When the consumer is the
    36	async webhook handler (Sprint H), a thin async adapter can be added
    37	without changing the public API.

   124	def _now_iso() -> str:
   125	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")

   128	def _make_fencing_token(instance_id: str) -> str:
   129	    """Per OP-977: ``claim:{instance}:{epoch_us}-{uuid}``."""
   130	    epoch_us = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1_000_000)
   131	    return f"claim:{instance_id}:{epoch_us}-{uuid.uuid4()}"

   136	    env_path = os.getenv("OMNISIGHT_DATABASE_PATH")
   137	    if env_path:
   138	        return Path(env_path)

   142	@contextmanager
   143	def _conn() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
   144	    """Open a sqlite3 connection with explicit transaction control.
   145	
   146	    ``isolation_level=None`` puts the connection in autocommit mode at
   147	    the driver layer; the caller manages BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK
   148	    explicitly via :meth:`sqlite3.Connection.execute`. This is the
   149	    pattern recommended by the sqlite3 stdlib docs for code that needs
   150	    explicit transaction boundaries.
   151	    """
   152	    db_path = _db_path()
   153	    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   154	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path), isolation_level=None, timeout=10.0)
   155	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
   156	    try:
   157	        yield conn
   158	    finally:
   159	        conn.close()
   160

   162	def _row_to_lease(row: sqlite3.Row) -> ClaimLease:
   163	    refs_raw = row["external_refs"]
   164	    try:
   165	        refs = json.loads(refs_raw) if isinstance(refs_raw, str) else (refs_raw or {})
   166	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
   167	        refs = {}
   168	    return ClaimLease(
   169	        lease_id=row["lease_id"],
   170	        ticket_key=row["ticket_key"],
   171	        resource_key=row["resource_key"],
   172	        owner_agent_class=row["owner_agent_class"],
   173	        owner_instance_id=row["owner_instance_id"],
   174	        fencing_token=row["fencing_token"],
   175	        state=row["state"],
   176	        phase=row["phase"],
   177	        heartbeat_at=row["heartbeat_at"],
   178	        acquired_at=row["acquired_at"],
   179	        released_at=row["released_at"],
   180	        release_reason=row["release_reason"],
   181	        external_refs=refs,
   182	    )

   188	def acquire_claim(
   189	    *,
   190	    ticket_key: str,
   191	    resource_key: str,
   192	    owner_agent_class: str,
   193	    owner_instance_id: str,
   194	    phase: str = "pickup",
   195	    external_refs: Optional[dict] = None,
   196	) -> ClaimLease:
   197	    """Atomically claim ``resource_key`` for ``ticket_key``.
   198	
   199	    Returns the resulting :class:`ClaimLease`. Raises
   200	    :class:`ClaimBlocked` (with ``existing_lease`` populated when
   201	    readable) if a different active lease holds ``resource_key``.
   202	
   203	    **Idempotency**: re-acquiring an existing active claim by the same
   204	    ``(ticket_key, resource_key, owner_agent_class, owner_instance_id)``
   205	    returns the existing lease unchanged — matching the OP-977
   206	    same-bot fast-fail behaviour. Different owner on a held resource
   207	    → :class:`ClaimBlocked`.
   208	    """
   209	    lease_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
   210	    fencing_token = _make_fencing_token(owner_instance_id)
   211	    now = _now_iso()
   212	    refs_json = json.dumps(external_refs or {})
   213	
   214	    with _conn() as conn:
   215	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
   216	        try:
   217	            row = conn.execute(
   218	                "SELECT * FROM runner_claims "
   219	                "WHERE resource_key = ? AND state = 'active' LIMIT 1",
   220	                (resource_key,),
   221	            ).fetchone()
   222	
   223	            if row is not None:
   224	                if (
   225	                    row["ticket_key"] == ticket_key
   226	                    and row["owner_agent_class"] == owner_agent_class
   227	                    and row["owner_instance_id"] == owner_instance_id
   228	                ):
   229	                    conn.execute("COMMIT")
   230	                    return _row_to_lease(row)
   230	                    return _row_to_lease(row)
   231	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   232	                raise ClaimBlocked(resource_key, _row_to_lease(row))
   233	
   234	            try:
   235	                conn.execute(
   236	                    "INSERT INTO runner_claims ("
   237	                    "lease_id, ticket_key, resource_key, owner_agent_class, "
   238	                    "owner_instance_id, fencing_token, state, phase, "
   239	                    "heartbeat_at, acquired_at, released_at, release_reason, "
   240	                    "external_refs) VALUES ("
   241	                    "?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'active', ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, ?)",
   242	                    (
   243	                        lease_id,
   244	                        ticket_key,
   245	                        resource_key,
   246	                        owner_agent_class,
   247	                        owner_instance_id,
   248	                        fencing_token,
   249	                        phase,
   250	                        now,
   251	                        now,
   252	                        refs_json,
   253	                    ),
   254	                )
   255	            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
   256	                # Partial unique index hit: another acquirer raced ahead
   257	                # between our SELECT and INSERT. Re-read to surface the
   258	                # winning lease.
   259	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   260	                row = conn.execute(
   261	                    "SELECT * FROM runner_claims "
   262	                    "WHERE resource_key = ? AND state = 'active' LIMIT 1",
   263	                    (resource_key,),
   264	                ).fetchone()
   265	                raise ClaimBlocked(resource_key, _row_to_lease(row) if row else None)
   266	
   267	            conn.execute("COMMIT")
   268	        except CoordinationError:
   269	            raise
   270	        except Exception:
   271	            try:
   272	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   273	            except sqlite3.Error:
   274	                pass
   275	            raise
   276	
   277	    return ClaimLease(
   278	        lease_id=lease_id,
   279	        ticket_key=ticket_key,
   280	        resource_key=resource_key,
   281	        owner_agent_class=owner_agent_class,
   282	        owner_instance_id=owner_instance_id,
   283	        fencing_token=fencing_token,
   284	        state="active",
   285	        phase=phase,
   286	        heartbeat_at=now,
   287	        acquired_at=now,
   288	        released_at=None,
   289	        release_reason=None,
   290	        external_refs=external_refs or {},
   291	    )

   293	
   294	def release_claim(
   295	    *,
   296	    lease_id: str,
   297	    fencing_token: str,
   298	    release_reason: str,
   299	) -> None:
   300	    """Release an active claim.
   301	
   302	    **Idempotency**: releasing an already-released lease (or one that
   303	    was never acquired) is a no-op — supports the "release in
   304	    ``finally``" runner pattern where the finally may fire on a path
   305	    that already released earlier.
   306	
   307	    Raises :class:`FencingTokenMismatch` if the active row exists but
   308	    its fencing_token does not match — protects against a stale lease
   309	    holder overwriting a fresh lease.
   310	    """
   311	    now = _now_iso()
   312	    with _conn() as conn:
   313	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
   314	        try:
   315	            row = conn.execute(
   316	                "SELECT fencing_token, state FROM runner_claims "
   317	                "WHERE lease_id = ? LIMIT 1",
   318	                (lease_id,),
   319	            ).fetchone()
   320	
   321	            if row is None:
   322	                conn.execute("COMMIT")
   323	                return
   324	            if row["state"] == "released":
   325	                conn.execute("COMMIT")
   326	                return
   327	            if row["fencing_token"] != fencing_token:
   328	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   329	                raise FencingTokenMismatch(lease_id)
   330	
   331	            conn.execute(
   332	                "UPDATE runner_claims SET state = 'released', "
   333	                "released_at = ?, release_reason = ? "
   334	                "WHERE lease_id = ? AND state = 'active'",
   335	                (now, release_reason, lease_id),
   336	            )
   337	            conn.execute("COMMIT")
   338	        except CoordinationError:
   339	            raise
   340	        except Exception:
   341	            try:
   342	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   343	            except sqlite3.Error:
   344	                pass
   345	            raise
   346	
   347	
   348	def record_phase(
   349	    *,
   350	    lease_id: str,
   351	    fencing_token: str,
   352	    phase: str,
   353	) -> None:
   354	    """Update ``phase`` and bump ``heartbeat_at`` on an active claim.
   355	
   356	    Raises :class:`ClaimNotFound` if no active claim exists.
   357	    Raises :class:`FencingTokenMismatch` if the fencing token doesn't
   358	    match the active row.
   359	    """
   360	    now = _now_iso()
   361	    with _conn() as conn:
   362	        row = conn.execute(
   363	            "SELECT fencing_token, state FROM runner_claims "
   364	            "WHERE lease_id = ? LIMIT 1",
   365	            (lease_id,),
   366	        ).fetchone()
   367	        if row is None or row["state"] != "active":
   368	            raise ClaimNotFound(lease_id)
   369	        if row["fencing_token"] != fencing_token:
   370	            raise FencingTokenMismatch(lease_id)
   371	        conn.execute(
   372	            "UPDATE runner_claims SET phase = ?, heartbeat_at = ? "
   373	            "WHERE lease_id = ? AND state = 'active'",
   374	            (phase, now, lease_id),
   375	        )

   302	class InMemoryQueueBackend:
   303	    """Single-process queue.  Thread-safe, FIFO within each priority class."""
   304	
   305	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   306	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   307	        # Ready queues by priority; each is a list of message_ids in FIFO order.
   308	        self._ready: dict[PriorityLevel, list[str]] = {
   309	            p: [] for p in PriorityLevel
   310	        }
   311	        # All messages keyed by id (queued, claimed, running, done, failed).
   312	        self._messages: dict[str, QueueMessage] = {}
   313	        # Claimed: message_id → (consumer, deadline)
   314	        self._claimed: set[str] = set()
   315	        self._dlq: dict[str, DlqEntry] = {}
   316	
   317	    # --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------
   318	
   319	    def _push_ready_locked(self, msg_id: str, priority: PriorityLevel) -> None:
   320	        # Maintain FIFO within priority + dedupe so re-enqueue doesn't pile up.
   321	        bucket = self._ready[priority]
   322	        if msg_id in bucket:
   323	            bucket.remove(msg_id)
   324	        bucket.append(msg_id)
   325	
   326	    def _record_state_locked(self, msg: QueueMessage, new: TaskState) -> None:
   327	        _check_transition(msg.state, new)
   328	        if msg.state != new:
   329	            msg.history.append((time.time(), new.value))
   330	            msg.state = new
   331	
   332	    # --- API -------------------------------------------------------
   333	
   334	    def push(self, card: TaskCard, priority: PriorityLevel) -> str:
   335	        msg_id = _new_message_id()
   336	        msg = QueueMessage(
   337	            message_id=msg_id,
   338	            priority=priority,
   339	            state=TaskState.Queued,
   340	            payload=card.to_dict(),
   341	            enqueued_at=time.time(),
   342	        )
   343	        msg.history.append((msg.enqueued_at, TaskState.Queued.value))
   344	        with self._lock:
   345	            self._messages[msg_id] = msg
   346	            self._push_ready_locked(msg_id, priority)
   347	        return msg_id
   348	
   349	    def pull(self, consumer: str, count: int,
   350	             visibility_timeout_s: float) -> list[QueueMessage]:
   351	        if count <= 0:
   352	            return []
   353	        out: list[QueueMessage] = []
   354	        now = time.time()
   355	        deadline = now + visibility_timeout_s
   356	        with self._lock:
   357	            for prio in PriorityLevel.ordered():       # P0 first
   358	                bucket = self._ready[prio]
   359	                while bucket and len(out) < count:
   360	                    msg_id = bucket.pop(0)
   361	                    msg = self._messages.get(msg_id)
   362	                    if msg is None:
   363	                        continue
   364	                    msg.delivery_count += 1
   365	                    msg.claim_owner = consumer
   366	                    msg.claim_deadline = deadline
   367	                    self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Claimed)
   368	                    self._claimed.add(msg_id)
   369	                    out.append(msg)
   370	                if len(out) >= count:
   371	                    break
   372	        return [self._copy(m) for m in out]
   373	
   374	    def ack(self, message_id: str) -> bool:
   375	        with self._lock:
   376	            msg = self._messages.get(message_id)
   377	            if msg is None:
   378	                return False
   379	            self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Done)
   380	            self._claimed.discard(message_id)
   381	            # Done is terminal → drop fully so memory doesn't grow.
   382	            del self._messages[message_id]
   383	            return True
   384	
   385	    def nack(self, message_id: str, reason: str,
   386	             stack: str | None = None) -> QueueMessage:
   387	        with self._lock:
   388	            msg = self._messages.get(message_id)
   389	            if msg is None:
   390	                raise MessageNotFound(message_id)
   391	            msg.last_error = reason
   392	            msg.last_error_stack = stack
   393	            self._claimed.discard(message_id)
   394	            if msg.delivery_count >= MAX_DELIVERIES:
   395	                self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Failed)
   396	                self._move_to_dlq_locked(msg, reason, stack)
   397	                del self._messages[message_id]
   398	                return self._copy(msg)
   399	            # Requeue at same priority.
   400	            self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Queued)
   401	            msg.claim_owner = None
   402	            msg.claim_deadline = 0.0
   403	            self._push_ready_locked(message_id, msg.priority)
   404	            return self._copy(msg)
   405	
   406	    def set_state(self, message_id: str, new_state: TaskState) -> QueueMessage:
   407	        with self._lock:
   408	            msg = self._messages.get(message_id)
   409	            if msg is None:
   410	                raise MessageNotFound(message_id)
   411	            self._record_state_locked(msg, new_state)
   412	            return self._copy(msg)
   413	
   414	    def get(self, message_id: str) -> QueueMessage | None:
   415	        with self._lock:
   416	            msg = self._messages.get(message_id)
   417	            return self._copy(msg) if msg else None
   418	
   419	    def depth(self, priority: PriorityLevel | None = None,
   420	              state: TaskState | None = None) -> int:
   421	        with self._lock:
   422	            if priority is None and state is None:
   423	                return len(self._messages)
   424	            n = 0
   425	            for msg in self._messages.values():
   426	                if priority is not None and msg.priority != priority:
   427	                    continue
   428	                if state is not None and msg.state != state:
   429	                    continue
   430	                n += 1
   431	            return n
   432	
   433	    def sweep_visibility(self, now: float | None = None) -> SweepResult:
   434	        started = time.time()
   435	        now = now if now is not None else started
   436	        requeued: list[str] = []
   437	        dlqd: list[str] = []
   438	        with self._lock:
   439	            for msg_id in list(self._claimed):
   440	                msg = self._messages.get(msg_id)
   441	                if msg is None:
   442	                    self._claimed.discard(msg_id)
   443	                    continue
   444	                if msg.claim_deadline > now:
   445	                    continue
   446	                # Visibility expired.
   447	                self._claimed.discard(msg_id)
   448	                if msg.delivery_count >= MAX_DELIVERIES:
   449	                    self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Failed)
   450	                    self._move_to_dlq_locked(
   451	                        msg, "visibility_timeout_exhausted", None,
   452	                    )
   453	                    del self._messages[msg_id]
   454	                    dlqd.append(msg_id)
   455	                else:
   456	                    msg.claim_owner = None
   457	                    msg.claim_deadline = 0.0
   458	                    self._record_state_locked(msg, TaskState.Queued)
   459	                    self._push_ready_locked(msg_id, msg.priority)
   460	                    requeued.append(msg_id)
   460	                    requeued.append(msg_id)
   461	        return SweepResult(
   462	            requeued_message_ids=requeued,
   463	            dlq_message_ids=dlqd,
   464	            elapsed_seconds=time.time() - started,
   465	        )
   466	
   467	    def dlq_list(self, limit: int) -> list[DlqEntry]:
   468	        with self._lock:
   469	            entries = sorted(
   470	                self._dlq.values(),
   471	                key=lambda e: e.moved_to_dlq_at,
   472	                reverse=True,
   473	            )
   474	            return [self._copy_dlq(e) for e in entries[:limit]]
   475	
   476	    def dlq_purge(self, message_id: str) -> bool:
   477	        with self._lock:
   478	            return self._dlq.pop(message_id, None) is not None
   479	
   480	    def dlq_redrive(self, message_id: str,
   481	                    new_priority: PriorityLevel | None = None) -> str:
   482	        with self._lock:
   483	            entry = self._dlq.pop(message_id, None)
   484	        if entry is None:
   485	            raise MessageNotFound(message_id)
   486	        prio = new_priority or entry.priority
   487	        card = TaskCard.from_dict(entry.payload)
   488	        return self.push(card, prio)
   489	
   490	    def clear_all(self) -> None:
   491	        with self._lock:
   492	            for bucket in self._ready.values():
   493	                bucket.clear()
   494	            self._messages.clear()
   495	            self._claimed.clear()
   496	            self._dlq.clear()
   497	
   498	    # --- internals -------------------------------------------------
   499	
   500	    def _move_to_dlq_locked(self, msg: QueueMessage, reason: str,
   501	                            stack: str | None) -> None:
   502	        entry = DlqEntry(
   503	            message_id=msg.message_id,
   504	            priority=msg.priority,
   505	            payload=msg.payload,
   506	            failure_count=msg.delivery_count,
   507	            root_cause=reason,
   508	            stack=stack,
   509	            moved_to_dlq_at=time.time(),
   510	            enqueued_at=msg.enqueued_at,
   511	        )
   512	        self._dlq[msg.message_id] = entry
   513	
   514	    @staticmethod
   515	    def _copy(msg: QueueMessage) -> QueueMessage:
   516	        return QueueMessage.from_dict(msg.to_dict())
   517	
   518	    @staticmethod
   519	    def _copy_dlq(entry: DlqEntry) -> DlqEntry:
   520	        return DlqEntry.from_dict(entry.to_dict())
   521	
   522	
   523	# ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   524	#  Redis Streams backend
   525	# ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   526	#
   527	# Redis schema:
   528	#
   529	#   ${KEY_PREFIX}stream:<priority>           XSTREAM   ready msgs (one per priority)
   530	#   ${KEY_PREFIX}group                       const consumer group name
   531	#   ${KEY_PREFIX}msg:<message_id>            HASH      authoritative msg state
   532	#   ${KEY_PREFIX}claimed                     ZSET      member=msg_id  score=deadline
   533	#   ${KEY_PREFIX}all                         SET       all live msg_ids
   534	#   ${DLQ_PREFIX}entries                     HASH      msg_id -> json(DlqEntry)
   535	#   ${DLQ_PREFIX}order                       ZSET      member=msg_id  score=ts
   536	#
   537	# Why streams (not LIST + BRPOP)?
   538	#   * Streams give you per-message ack semantics + claim tracking
   539	#     (XPENDING / XCLAIM) — visibility-timeout sweep is a Redis-native
   540	#     primitive on streams.
   541	#   * Multiple consumers in the same consumer group automatically share
   542	#     load without us having to write our own dispatch.
   543	
   544	_GROUP_NAME = "omnisight-workers"
   545	_CONSUMER_LEASE_S = 24 * 3600   # XINFO entry TTL hint
   546	
   547	
   548	class RedisStreamsQueueBackend:
   549	    """Redis Streams + ancillary hashes implementation.
   550	
   551	    All queue-side state lives in Redis so multiple workers / hosts can
   552	    share the same view.  The single source of truth for any message's
   553	    state machine + delivery_count + last_error is the per-message
   554	    HASH; the priority XSTREAMs are just the dispatcher.
   555	    """
   556	
   557	    def __init__(self, redis_url: str) -> None:
   558	        import redis as _redis
   559	        self._pool = _redis.ConnectionPool.from_url(
   560	            redis_url, decode_responses=True,
   561	        )
   562	        self._client = _redis.Redis(connection_pool=self._pool)
   563	        # Ensure the consumer group exists for every priority stream.
   564	        for prio in PriorityLevel.ordered():
   565	            stream_key = self._stream_key(prio)
   566	            try:
   567	                self._client.xgroup_create(
   568	                    name=stream_key, groupname=_GROUP_NAME,
   569	                    id="0", mkstream=True,
   570	                )
   571	            except _redis.ResponseError as exc:
   572	                # BUSYGROUP — already exists.
   573	                if "BUSYGROUP" not in str(exc):
   574	                    raise
   575	
   576	    # --- key helpers ----------------------------------------------
   577	
   578	    def _stream_key(self, prio: PriorityLevel) -> str:
   579	        return f"{KEY_PREFIX}stream:{prio.value}"
   580	
   581	    def _msg_key(self, msg_id: str) -> str:
   582	        return f"{KEY_PREFIX}msg:{msg_id}"
   583	
   584	    def _claimed_zset(self) -> str:
   585	        return f"{KEY_PREFIX}claimed"
   586	
   587	    def _all_set(self) -> str:
   588	        return f"{KEY_PREFIX}all"
   589	
   590	    def _dlq_hash(self) -> str:
   591	        return f"{DLQ_PREFIX}entries"
   592	
   593	    def _dlq_zset(self) -> str:
   594	        return f"{DLQ_PREFIX}order"
   595	
   596	    def _read_msg(self, msg_id: str) -> QueueMessage | None:
   597	        raw = self._client.hgetall(self._msg_key(msg_id))
   598	        if not raw:
   599	            return None
   600	        return QueueMessage(
   601	            message_id=msg_id,
   602	            priority=PriorityLevel(raw["priority"]),
   603	            state=TaskState(raw["state"]),
   604	            payload=json.loads(raw["payload"]),
   605	            enqueued_at=float(raw["enqueued_at"]),
   606	            delivery_count=int(raw.get("delivery_count", "0") or 0),
   607	            claim_owner=raw.get("claim_owner") or None,
   608	            claim_deadline=float(raw.get("claim_deadline", "0") or 0),
   609	            last_error=raw.get("last_error") or None,
   610	            last_error_stack=raw.get("last_error_stack") or None,
   611	            history=json.loads(raw.get("history", "[]") or "[]"),
   612	        )
   613	
   614	    def _write_msg(self, msg: QueueMessage) -> None:
   615	        self._client.hset(self._msg_key(msg.message_id), mapping={
   616	            "priority": msg.priority.value,
   617	            "state": msg.state.value,
   618	            "payload": json.dumps(msg.payload),
   619	            "enqueued_at": str(msg.enqueued_at),
   620	            "delivery_count": str(msg.delivery_count),
   621	            "claim_owner": msg.claim_owner or "",
   622	            "claim_deadline": str(msg.claim_deadline),
   623	            "last_error": msg.last_error or "",
   624	            "last_error_stack": msg.last_error_stack or "",
   625	            "history": json.dumps([list(h) for h in msg.history]),
   626	        })
   627	
   628	    def _record_state(self, msg: QueueMessage, new: TaskState) -> None:
   629	        _check_transition(msg.state, new)
   630	        if msg.state != new:
   631	            msg.history.append((time.time(), new.value))
   632	            msg.state = new
   633	
   634	    # --- API ------------------------------------------------------
   635	
   636	    def push(self, card: TaskCard, priority: PriorityLevel) -> str:
   637	        msg_id = _new_message_id()
   638	        now = time.time()
   639	        msg = QueueMessage(
   640	            message_id=msg_id,
   641	            priority=priority,
   642	            state=TaskState.Queued,
   643	            payload=card.to_dict(),
   644	            enqueued_at=now,
   645	            history=[(now, TaskState.Queued.value)],
   646	        )
   647	        self._write_msg(msg)
   648	        self._client.sadd(self._all_set(), msg_id)
   649	        self._client.xadd(self._stream_key(priority), {"id": msg_id})
   650	        return msg_id
   651	
   652	    def pull(self, consumer: str, count: int,
   653	             visibility_timeout_s: float) -> list[QueueMessage]:
   654	        if count <= 0:
   655	            return []
   656	        deadline = time.time() + visibility_timeout_s
   657	        out: list[QueueMessage] = []
   658	        for prio in PriorityLevel.ordered():       # P0 first
   659	            if len(out) >= count:
   660	                break
   661	            need = count - len(out)
   662	            stream_key = self._stream_key(prio)
   663	            try:
   664	                resp = self._client.xreadgroup(
   665	                    groupname=_GROUP_NAME, consumername=consumer,
   666	                    streams={stream_key: ">"}, count=need, block=0,
   667	                )
   668	            except Exception as exc:
   669	                logger.warning("O2 queue: xreadgroup(%s) failed: %s",
   670	                               stream_key, exc)
   671	                continue
   672	            if not resp:
   673	                continue
   674	            for _stream, entries in resp:
   675	                for entry_id, fields in entries:
   676	                    msg_id = fields.get("id")
   677	                    if not msg_id:
   678	                        # Unknown stream entry — ack & drop so we don't loop.
   679	                        self._client.xack(stream_key, _GROUP_NAME, entry_id)
   680	                        continue
   681	                    msg = self._read_msg(msg_id)
   682	                    if msg is None:
   683	                        self._client.xack(stream_key, _GROUP_NAME, entry_id)
   684	                        continue
   685	                    msg.delivery_count += 1
   686	                    msg.claim_owner = consumer
   687	                    msg.claim_deadline = deadline
   688	                    self._record_state(msg, TaskState.Claimed)
   689	                    self._write_msg(msg)
   690	                    self._client.zadd(self._claimed_zset(), {msg_id: deadline})
   691	                    # Stash stream entry id so ack can XACK it later.
   692	                    self._client.hset(
   693	                        self._msg_key(msg_id),
   694	                        mapping={"_stream_key": stream_key, "_entry_id": entry_id},
   695	                    )
   696	                    out.append(msg)
   697	        return out
   698	
   699	    def ack(self, message_id: str) -> bool:
   700	        raw = self._client.hgetall(self._msg_key(message_id))
   701	        if not raw:
   702	            return False
   703	        stream_key = raw.get("_stream_key")
   704	        entry_id = raw.get("_entry_id")
   705	        if stream_key and entry_id:
   706	            try:
   707	                self._client.xack(stream_key, _GROUP_NAME, entry_id)
   708	                self._client.xdel(stream_key, entry_id)
   709	            except Exception as exc:
   710	                logger.warning("O2 queue: xack(%s/%s) failed: %s",
   711	                               stream_key, entry_id, exc)
   712	        self._client.delete(self._msg_key(message_id))
   713	        self._client.srem(self._all_set(), message_id)
   714	        self._client.zrem(self._claimed_zset(), message_id)
   715	        return True
   716	
   717	    def nack(self, message_id: str, reason: str,
   718	             stack: str | None = None) -> QueueMessage:
   719	        msg = self._read_msg(message_id)
   720	        if msg is None:

   280	class LocalSandboxRuntime:
   281	    """Filesystem sandbox.  No Docker required.
   282	
   283	    ``start`` materialises a fresh workspace directory + clones a thin
   284	    tree containing **only** the files matched by the CATC card's
   285	    ``impact_scope.allowed`` globs.  Anything else (other source tree,
   286	    secrets, sibling repos) is physically unreachable from the
   287	    workspace because it was never copied in.
   288	
   289	    The worker uses ``git`` inside the workspace to commit; ``commit``
   290	    runs ``git add -A && git commit -m ...`` in the workspace dir and
   291	    returns the resulting SHA.  This keeps the local backend trivially
   292	    testable while preserving the spec's "bind-mount only allowed
   293	    paths" guarantee (the implementation IS the bind, just via copy).
   294	    """
   295	
   296	    def __init__(self, *, workdir_root: Path | None = None,
   297	                 init_git: bool = True) -> None:
   298	        self._root = Path(workdir_root or
   299	                          os.environ.get("OMNISIGHT_WORKER_WORKDIR")
   300	                          or Path.cwd() / ".artifacts" / "worker_sandboxes")
   301	        self._init_git = init_git
   302	        self._root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   303	
   304	    def start(self, *, worker_id: str, task_id: str,
   305	              card: TaskCard, project_root: Path) -> SandboxHandle:
   306	        ws = self._root / f"{worker_id}-{task_id}"
   307	        if ws.exists():
   308	            _rmtree(ws)
   309	        ws.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   310	
   311	        allowed = list(card.navigation.impact_scope.allowed)
   312	        copied: list[str] = []
   313	        for glob in allowed:
   314	            for src in _resolve_glob(project_root, glob):
   315	                rel = src.relative_to(project_root)
   316	                dst = ws / rel
   317	                dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   318	                if src.is_dir():
   319	                    _copytree(src, dst)
   320	                else:
   321	                    _copyfile(src, dst)
   322	                copied.append(str(rel))
   323	
   324	        if self._init_git:
   325	            _run_git(ws, ["init", "-q", "-b", "main"])
   326	            _run_git(ws, ["config", "user.name", f"omnisight-worker-{worker_id}"])
   327	            _run_git(ws, ["config", "user.email",
   328	                          f"{worker_id}@omnisight.local"])
   329	            if copied:
   330	                _run_git(ws, ["add", "-A"])
   331	                _run_git(ws, ["commit", "--allow-empty", "-q",
   332	                              "-m", f"baseline: {card.jira_ticket}"])
   333	
   334	        return SandboxHandle(
   335	            workspace=ws,
   336	            runtime_id="local",
   337	            metadata={"copied": copied, "task_id": task_id},
   338	        )
   339	
   340	    def commit(self, handle: SandboxHandle, *,
   341	               commit_message: str) -> str:
   342	        if not self._init_git:
   343	            return ""
   344	        _run_git(handle.workspace, ["add", "-A"])
   345	        rc, out, err = _run_git(handle.workspace,
   346	                                ["commit", "--allow-empty", "-q",
   347	                                 "-m", commit_message])
   348	        if rc != 0:
   349	            raise RuntimeError(
   350	                f"sandbox commit failed: {err.strip() or out.strip()}"
   351	            )
   352	        rc, sha, _ = _run_git(handle.workspace, ["rev-parse", "HEAD"])
   353	        if rc != 0:
   354	            raise RuntimeError("sandbox commit succeeded but rev-parse failed")
   355	        return sha.strip()
   356	
   357	    def stop(self, handle: SandboxHandle) -> None:
   358	        try:
   359	            _rmtree(handle.workspace)
   360	        except OSError as exc:
   361	            logger.warning("sandbox cleanup failed for %s: %s",
   362	                           handle.workspace, exc)

   392	class GerritCommandPusher:
   393	    """Production pusher — uses the local ``git`` CLI to push to
   394	    ``refs/for/main`` (Gerrit's "review" magic ref).
   395	
   396	    The class is intentionally thin: it shells out to ``git push``
   397	    against the workspace's git directory so the real git protocol
   398	    handles auth (SSH key on the agent host).  Retries are bounded
   399	    (``GERRIT_PUSH_MAX_RETRIES``) with backoff — Gerrit transient
   400	    errors (network, 503) shouldn't kill the queue ack.
   401	    """
   402	
   403	    def __init__(self, *, remote: str = "origin",
   404	                 ref: str = "refs/for/main",
   405	                 max_retries: int = GERRIT_PUSH_MAX_RETRIES,
   406	                 backoff_s: tuple[float, ...] = GERRIT_PUSH_BACKOFF_S,
   407	                 runner: Callable[..., tuple[int, str, str]] | None = None
   408	                 ) -> None:
   409	        self._remote = remote
   410	        self._ref = ref
   411	        self._max_retries = max(1, max_retries)
   412	        self._backoff = backoff_s
   413	        # Injectable so tests can simulate transient failures.
   414	        self._runner = runner or _run_git
   415	
   416	    def push(self, *, handle: SandboxHandle, card: TaskCard,
   417	             commit_sha: str, change_id: str,
   418	             worker_id: str) -> GerritPushResult:
   419	        last_err = ""
   420	        for attempt in range(1, self._max_retries + 1):
   421	            rc, out, err = self._runner(
   422	                handle.workspace,
   423	                ["push", self._remote, f"HEAD:{self._ref}"],
   424	            )
   425	            if rc == 0:
   426	                return GerritPushResult(
   427	                    ok=True,
   428	                    change_id=change_id,
   429	                    review_url=_extract_review_url(out + "\n" + err),
   430	                    attempts=attempt,
   431	                )
   432	            last_err = (err or out).strip()
   433	            logger.warning(
   434	                "Gerrit push attempt %d/%d for %s failed: %s",
   435	                attempt, self._max_retries, card.jira_ticket, last_err,

     4

     6	    pipeline_phase / decision_chain / report-gen).
     7	  - `workflow_steps` append-only checkpoint log; (run_id,
     8	    idempotency_key) UNIQUE so repeating the same step returns the
